lists.head: skandha
lists.summary_zh: 佛陀將有情身心分析為色、受、想、行、識五類聚合，以顯示其中無我。五蘊總攝一切有為法。
lists.summary_en: The Buddha's analysis of a person into five groups — form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — to show that none of them is a self. Together they cover all conditioned dharmas.

lists.head: sarvatraga
lists.summary_zh: 百法五十一心所的第一位：任何一念心生起時必定具有的五個心所。次序依《大乘百法明門論》：作意、觸、受、想、思（《成唯識論》作觸、作意、受、想、思）。
lists.summary_en: The first of the six categories of the 51 mental factors — the five present in every moment of mind. Order follows the Hundred Dharmas treatise (attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition); the Cheng weishi lun lists contact first.

lists.summary_zh: 理解五蘊、心所與十二因緣所需的基礎名相。
lists.summary_en: Core terms needed to understand the aggregates, the mental factors and dependent origination.

lists.summary_zh: 只在緣特定對象時才生起的五個心所：欲（所樂境）、勝解（決定境）、念（曾習境）、定與慧（所觀境）。
lists.summary_en: Five factors that arise only with particular kinds of object: aspiration (desired), resolve (ascertained), mindfulness (familiar), concentration and wisdom (observed).

lists.summary_zh: 唯在善心中生起的十一個心所，各有所對治的煩惱。其中不放逸、行捨、不害是依他法假立。
lists.summary_en: The eleven factors found only in wholesome minds, each counteracting an affliction. Conscientiousness, equanimity and non-harming are designated on other factors.

lists.summary_zh: 貪、瞋、慢、無明（癡）、疑、不正見（惡見）——一切煩惱的根本，隨煩惱皆由此分出。
lists.summary_en: Greed, aversion, pride, ignorance, doubt and wrong view — the roots from which the secondary afflictions derive.

lists.summary_zh: 根本煩惱的分位或等流。小隨十（各別起）、中隨二（遍不善心）、大隨八（遍一切染心）。
lists.summary_en: Phases or outflows of the root afflictions: ten minor (arising separately), two intermediate (in every unwholesome mind), eight major (in every defiled mind).

lists.summary_zh: 惡作（悔）、睡眠、尋、伺——善、惡、無記不定，隨所伴隨的心而定其性質。
lists.summary_en: Regret, sleep, initial inquiry and sustained investigation — their moral quality depends on the mind they accompany.

terms.root: √rañj「染色、染著」 · √rañj "to be dyed, coloured, attached"
terms.short_zh: 對三有及其因染著；能障無貪，生起苦果。六根本煩惱之首，三毒之一。
terms.short_en: Greed — attachment to existence and its causes; obstructs non-greed and produces suffering. First root affliction, one of the three poisons.
terms.detail_zh:
rāga 原義是「染色」——心被對象「染上顏色」而黏著。《成唯識論》：「於有、有具，染著為性；能障無貪，生苦為業。」《大乘五蘊論》說得更具體：「於五取蘊染愛耽著為性。」

「生苦為業」：由愛著而生取，由取而造業，由業而受苦果——這正是十二因緣中「受緣愛、愛緣取」的環節。十二因緣的「愛」（tṛṣṇā）即貪的一種表現。

貪與瞋、癡合稱**三毒**、**三不善根**。依所貪之境分為欲貪、色貪、無色貪。隨煩惱中的慳、憍即以貪為體（「貪愛一分」）。
terms.detail_en:
Rāga originally means "dye": the mind is "coloured" by its object and sticks to it. Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is attachment to existence and the means of existence; it obstructs non-greed and produces suffering." The Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is passionate love of and absorption in the five aggregates of clinging."

"Produces suffering": attachment leads to clinging, clinging to karma, karma to painful results — the links "feeling → craving → clinging" of dependent origination. The craving (tṛṣṇā) of the twelve links is one expression of greed.

With hatred and delusion it forms the **three poisons** or **three unwholesome roots**. By object it is greed for the desire, form or formless realms. The secondary afflictions stinginess and haughtiness are "parts of greed".

quotes.text: 云何為貪？於有、有具，染著為性；能障無貪，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is greed? Its nature is attachment to existence and the means of existence; its function is to obstruct non-greed and produce suffering.

quotes.text: 云何為貪？謂於五取蘊染愛耽著為性。
quotes.note_en: What is greed? Its nature is passionate love of and absorption in the five aggregates of clinging.

quotes.text: 多欲之人多求利故，苦惱亦多；
quotes.source_en: Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching (Yijiao jing)
quotes.note_en: People of many desires seek much gain, and so their suffering is also great.

terms.root: prati-√han「反擊、抵觸」 · prati-√han "to strike back, repel"
terms.short_zh: 對苦及苦因憎恚，令身心不安，是惡行的所依。三毒之一。
terms.short_en: Aversion — hostility toward suffering and its causes; it makes one uneasy and is the basis of misconduct. One of the three poisons.
terms.detail_zh:
pratigha 字面是「反擊、抵觸」。《成唯識論》：「於苦、苦具，憎恚為性；能障無瞋，不安隱性，惡行所依為業。」瞋一起，身心便熱惱不安，並成為種種惡行的依據。《大乘五蘊論》：「於有情樂作損害為性。」

瞋有許多「分支」：隨煩惱中的忿、恨、惱、嫉、害五者，都是「瞋恚一分為體」，只是在不同情境下的表現（見比較卡「瞋的五種分位」）。

《遺教經》：「瞋恚之害，能破諸善法、壞好名聞。」
terms.detail_en:
Pratigha literally means "striking back, repulsion". Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is hostility toward suffering and the causes of suffering; it obstructs non-hatred, brings unease, and is the basis of misconduct." Once aversion arises, body and mind burn and become unsettled, and it serves as the basis for harmful acts. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is delighting in harming beings."

Aversion has several "branches": the secondary afflictions wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy and harmfulness are all "parts of aversion", its forms in particular situations (see the comparison card).

The Yijiao jing: "The harm of anger destroys all good dharmas and ruins a good name."

quotes.text: 云何為瞋？於苦、苦具，憎恚為性；能障無瞋，不安隱性，惡行所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is aversion? Its nature is hostility toward suffering and its causes; its function is to obstruct non-hatred, to cause unease, and to be the basis of misconduct.

quotes.text: 云何為瞋？謂於有情樂作損害為性。
quotes.note_en: What is aversion? Its nature is delighting in harming sentient beings.

quotes.text: 瞋恚之害能破諸善法、壞好名聞
quotes.source_en: Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching (Yijiao jing)
quotes.note_en: The harm of anger destroys all good dharmas and ruins a good name.

terms.root: √man「思量、自認為」 · √man "to think, consider (oneself)"
terms.short_zh: 仗恃自己、對他人心起高舉；能障不慢，生苦。有七慢之分。
terms.short_en: Pride — relying on oneself and holding oneself above others; obstructs humility and produces suffering. Seven kinds.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「恃己於他，高舉為性；能障不慢，生苦為業。」慢的核心是**比較**：拿自己和他人比，而心生高舉。

《大乘五蘊論》列**七慢**：慢（於劣計己勝、於等計己等）、過慢（於等計己勝）、慢過慢（於勝計己勝）、我慢（執五取蘊為我而高舉）、增上慢（未證謂證）、卑慢（於多分殊勝計己少分下劣而仍高舉）、邪慢（無德謂有德）。

其中**我慢**最根本，第七末那識恆與我慢相應。慢與隨煩惱的「憍」不同：慢要和他人比較，憍是對自己的盛事陶醉，不必比較（見比較卡）。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Relying on oneself, its nature is to hold oneself high over others; it obstructs humility and produces suffering." The essence of māna is **comparison**: measuring oneself against others and rising above them.

The Pañcaskandhaka lists **seven kinds**: pride (thinking oneself better than inferiors or equal to equals), excessive pride (better than equals), pride beyond pride (better than superiors), pride of "I am" (taking the aggregates as self), conceit of attainment (claiming realization not reached), deprecating pride (still puffed up while admitting one is a little inferior to those far superior), and wrong pride (claiming virtues one lacks).

**Pride of "I am"** is the most fundamental; the seventh consciousness, manas, is always accompanied by it. Pride differs from haughtiness (mada): pride compares with others, haughtiness is self-intoxication with one's own fortune, needing no comparison.

quotes.text: 云何為慢？恃己於他，高舉為性；能障不慢，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is pride? Relying on oneself, its nature is holding oneself high over others; its function is to obstruct humility and produce suffering.

quotes.text: 所謂七慢：一、慢，二、過慢，三、慢過慢，四、我慢，五、增上慢，六、卑慢，七、邪慢。
quotes.note_en: Namely the seven kinds of pride: 1 pride, 2 excessive pride, 3 pride beyond pride, 4 pride of "I am", 5 conceit of attainment, 6 deprecating pride, 7 wrong pride.

terms.root: vi-√cit 的願望式「想辨清而不能」 · desiderative of vi-√cit, "wanting to discern (but failing)"
terms.short_zh: 對四諦等真理猶豫不決；能障「不疑」的善品。
terms.short_en: Doubt — vacillation about the truths; obstructs wholesome states of certainty.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於諸諦理，猶豫為性；能障不疑善品為業。」這裡的疑專指對四諦、業果、三寶等**真理**的猶豫；一般生活中的不確定（例如不知道路怎麼走）不屬煩惱之疑。

疑之所以是根本煩惱，是因為它讓人停在岔路口，不肯踏上修行之路。《大智度論》喻：「如人在岐道，疑惑無所趣。」

疑與勝解相對：勝解於決定境印持不移；疑則於真理不能決定。疑是「分別起」的煩惱，由思惟分別而生，見道時即斷。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is vacillation about the truths; it obstructs the wholesome states of non-doubt." It concerns **the truths** — the four noble truths, karma and its result, the Three Jewels; ordinary uncertainty (not knowing the way home) is not the affliction of doubt.

Doubt is a root affliction because it leaves one standing at the crossroads, unwilling to set out on the path. The Dazhidu lun: "like a man at a fork in the road, doubtful, going nowhere."

Doubt is the opposite of resolve: resolve holds firmly to what is ascertained; doubt cannot decide about the truth. It is an affliction "arising from conceptualization", abandoned at the path of seeing.

quotes.text: 云何為疑？於諸諦理，猶豫為性；能障不疑善品為業。
quotes.note_en: What is doubt? Its nature is vacillation about the truths; its function is to obstruct the wholesome states of non-doubt.

quotes.text: 云何為疑？謂於諦等猶豫為性。
quotes.note_en: What is doubt? Its nature is vacillation about the truths and so on.

quotes.text: 如人在岐道，疑惑無所趣；諸法實相中，疑亦復如是。
quotes.note_en: Like a man at a fork in the road, doubtful and going nowhere — so is doubt with regard to the true nature of dharmas.

terms.root: √dṛś「看」→「見解」 · √dṛś "to see": view, opinion
terms.short_zh: 對諸諦理顛倒推度的染污之慧；能障善見，招苦。分為五見。
terms.short_en: Wrong view — defiled discernment that reasons perversely about the truths; obstructs right view and brings suffering. Five kinds.
terms.detail_zh:
百法稱「不正見」，《成唯識論》稱「惡見」：「於諸諦理，顛倒推度，染慧為性；能障善見，招苦為業。」注意它的體性是**染慧**——惡見不是缺乏思考，而是用錯誤的方式推理。

《大乘五蘊論》列**五見**：
1. **薩迦耶見**（身見）：於五取蘊執為我、我所；
2. **邊執見**：隨身見而執常或斷；
3. **邪見**：謗因、謗果、謗作用、壞善事；
4. **見取**：執以上諸見為最勝；
5. **戒禁取**：執錯誤的戒律禁制為清淨解脫之道。

梵語單說 dṛṣṭi 只是「見解」，在煩惱脈絡中才指錯誤的見；八正道的「正見」（samyag-dṛṣṭi）則是正確的見。

quotes.text: 云何惡見？於諸諦理，顛倒推度，染慧為性；能障善見，招苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is bad view? Its nature is defiled discernment that reasons perversely about the truths; its function is to obstruct good view and bring suffering.

quotes.text: 所謂五見：一、薩迦耶見，二、邊執見，三、邪見，四、見取，五、戒禁取。
quotes.note_en: Namely the five views: 1 view of a real self, 2 extreme views, 3 wrong view, 4 holding views as supreme, 5 holding rules and rituals as supreme.

quotes.text: 云何薩迦耶見？謂於五取蘊隨觀為我或為我所，染污慧為性。
quotes.note_en: What is the view of a real self? Taking the five aggregates of clinging as I or mine; its nature is defiled discernment.

terms.root: √krudh「發怒」 · √krudh "to be angry"
terms.short_zh: 對當前不利之境憤然發作，乃至動手；以瞋為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Wrath — flaring up at a present harmful situation, to the point of violence; a part of aversion. A minor secondary affliction.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「依對現前不饒益境，憤發為性；能障不忿，執杖為業。」忿是瞋的**當下爆發**：面對眼前不利於己的人事，怒氣衝上來，甚至「執杖」動手。

體性：「此即瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿相用故。」忿沒有獨立實體，是瞋在特定情境的表現。忿過後懷恨不捨就成「恨」，恨再引發惡言便是「惱」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is flaring up at a present unbeneficial object; it obstructs non-wrath and its function is taking up the stick." Wrath is aversion **erupting in the moment**: faced with someone or something harmful right now, anger surges, even to violence.

Substance: "It is a part of aversion; apart from aversion wrath has no characteristic or function." It follows that wrath held on to becomes resentment, and resentment breaking out in harsh words becomes spite.

quotes.text: 云何為忿？依對現前不饒益境，憤發為性；能障不忿，執杖為業。
quotes.note_en: What is wrath? In the face of a present unbeneficial object, its nature is flaring up; its function is to obstruct non-wrath and take up the stick.

quotes.text: 此即瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿相用故。
quotes.note_en: It has a part of aversion as its substance; apart from aversion there is no separate characteristic or function of wrath.

terms.root: upa-√nah「綁住、結」 · upa-√nah "to tie up, bind"
terms.short_zh: 忿後懷惡不捨、結怨在心，令人熱惱；以瞋為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Resentment — after wrath, holding on to ill will and nursing a grudge, which burns within; a part of aversion.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「由忿為先，懷惡不捨，結怨為性；能障不恨，熱惱為業。」梵語 upanāha 意為「綁住」——把怨氣綁在心上，不肯放下。

忿是一時的爆發，恨是**持續的積怨**。「熱惱為業」：懷恨的人自己先被這股怨氣燒灼，不得安寧。體性同樣是「瞋恚一分」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Preceded by wrath, holding on to malice without letting go, its nature is binding enmity; it obstructs non-resentment and its function is burning vexation." Upanāha means "tying up": anger bound to the heart, never released.

Wrath is a momentary outburst; resentment is **lasting grievance**. Its function "burning vexation" means the resentful person is the first to be scorched. Its substance is likewise a part of aversion.

quotes.text: 云何為恨？由忿為先，懷惡不捨，結怨為性；能障不恨，熱惱為業。
quotes.note_en: What is resentment? Preceded by wrath, holding on to malice without letting go, its nature is binding enmity; its function is to obstruct non-resentment and cause burning vexation.

quotes.text: 云何為恨？謂結怨不捨為性。
quotes.note_en: What is resentment? Its nature is binding enmity and not letting it go.

terms.root: pra-√daś「咬、螫」 · pra-√daṃś "to bite"
terms.short_zh: 由忿、恨引發，暴躁乖戾，以惡言螫人；以瞋為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Spite — arising from wrath and resentment, becoming vicious and lashing out with stinging words; a part of aversion.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「忿、恨為先，追觸暴熱，佷戾為性；能障不惱，䖧螫為業。」惱是在忿與恨之後，追憶往事、觸動舊怨，心變得暴躁乖戾，於是像蠍子般「螫」人——多半表現為尖刻的言語。《大乘五蘊論》：「發暴惡言尤䖧為性。」

忿→恨→惱，是瞋在時間上逐步發展的三個階段。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Preceded by wrath and resentment, recalling and touching old grievances, fierce and hot, its nature is perverse viciousness; it obstructs non-spite and its function is stinging." After wrath and resentment, brooding on the past stirs up old grudges; the mind turns fierce and one "stings" like a scorpion — usually in cutting words. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is uttering violent, abusive words."

Wrath → resentment → spite are three stages in the development of aversion over time.

quotes.text: 云何為惱？忿、恨為先，追觸暴熱，佷戾為性；能障不惱，䖧螫為業。
quotes.note_en: What is spite? Preceded by wrath and resentment, recalling and touching [grievances], fierce and hot, its nature is perversity; its function is to obstruct non-spite and to sting.

quotes.text: 云何為惱？謂發暴惡言尤䖧為性。
quotes.note_en: What is spite? Its nature is uttering violent, abusive, stinging words.

terms.root: √mrakṣ「塗抹、掩蓋」 · √mrakṣ "to smear over, conceal"
terms.short_zh: 怕失去利益名譽而隱藏自己的罪過，後來悔惱不安。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Concealment — hiding one's own wrongdoing for fear of losing gain and reputation, later tormented by regret.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於自作罪，恐失利、譽，隱藏為性；能障不覆，悔惱為業。」覆的重點是「**藏自己的過錯**」，動機是保護名利。「悔惱為業」：藏著的罪讓人日後內心不安。

體性：論中諸說，一說「癡一分攝」，一說「貪、癡一分為體」——因怕失名利（貪）而不懂得發露懺悔（癡）。

覆、誑、諂三者都涉及欺瞞，但方向不同：覆是隱藏自己有的過失，誑是假裝自己沒有的德行，諂是為了籠絡他人而扭曲自己（見比較卡）。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is hiding one's own wrongdoing for fear of losing gain and reputation; it obstructs non-concealment and its function is remorseful vexation." The point is **hiding one's own faults**, motivated by protecting one's standing; the hidden wrong later gnaws at the mind.

Substance: the treatise records views that it is a part of delusion, or of greed and delusion — fearing loss of reputation (greed) and not knowing to confess (delusion).

Concealment, deceit and guile all involve deception but point differently: concealment hides faults one has; deceit pretends to virtues one lacks; guile twists oneself to ensnare others (see the comparison card).

quotes.text: 云何為覆？於自作罪，恐失利、譽，隱藏為性；能障不覆，悔惱為業。
quotes.note_en: What is concealment? Its nature is hiding one's own wrongdoing for fear of losing gain and reputation; its function is to obstruct non-concealment and cause remorseful vexation.

quotes.text: 云何為覆？謂於自罪覆藏為性。
quotes.note_en: What is concealment? Its nature is hiding one's own wrongdoing.

terms.root: 「幻術、幻化」 · "magic, illusion"
terms.short_zh: 為求利養名譽，偽裝自己有德行；由此邪命自活。以貪、癡為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Deceit — feigning virtues one lacks in order to gain profit and fame, leading to wrong livelihood; a part of greed and delusion.
terms.detail_zh:
māyā 原義是「幻術」——像魔術師變出不存在的東西。《成唯識論》：「為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；能障不誑，邪命為業。」誑是**假裝有德**來騙取供養與名聲，所以「邪命為業」——以不正當的方式謀生。

體性：「此即貪、癡一分為體，離二無別誑相用故。」
terms.detail_en:
Māyā originally means "magic, illusion" — conjuring up what is not there. Cheng weishi lun: "To obtain profit and fame, its nature is feigning virtues with trickery; it obstructs non-deceit and its function is wrong livelihood." Deceit is **pretending to virtue** to win offerings and renown, hence "wrong livelihood".

Substance: "It is a part of greed and delusion; apart from these two it has no characteristic or function."

quotes.text: 云何為誑？為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；能障不誑，邪命為業。
quotes.note_en: What is deceit? For the sake of profit and fame, its nature is feigning virtue with trickery; its function is to obstruct non-deceit and lead to wrong livelihood.

quotes.text: 云何為誑？謂為誑他詐現不實事為性。
quotes.note_en: What is deceit? Its nature is feigning what is not real in order to deceive others.

terms.root: śaṭha「狡詐」 · śaṭha "crafty, false"
terms.short_zh: 為籠絡他人而曲意逢迎、隱藏真相，心不正直；以貪、癡為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Guile — twisting oneself to ensnare others, fawning and hiding the truth; a crooked mind. A part of greed and delusion.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「為網他故，矯設異儀，險、曲為性；能障不諂教誨為業。」「網他」即設網籠絡別人：為了討好或利用他人而刻意做出種種姿態，心術險曲。

「能障不諂教誨」：諂曲的人連師友的正直教誨也聽不進去，因為他總在揣摩、掩飾。《大乘五蘊論》：「覆藏自過方便所攝心曲為性。」體性同樣是「貪、癡一分」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "In order to net others, it contrives unusual manners; its nature is dangerous crookedness; its function is to obstruct non-guile and [receptivity to] instruction." To "net others" is to lay traps: putting on appearances to please or use people.

Obstructing instruction: the guileful cannot take in the straightforward advice of teachers and friends, since they are always calculating and covering. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is crookedness of mind, a means of hiding one's faults." Its substance too is a part of greed and delusion.

quotes.text: 云何為諂？為網他故，矯設異儀，險、曲為性；能障不諂教誨為業。
quotes.note_en: What is guile? To net others, it contrives unusual manners; its nature is dangerous crookedness; its function is to obstruct non-guile and instruction.

quotes.text: 云何為諂？謂覆藏自過方便所攝心曲為性。
quotes.note_en: What is guile? Its nature is crookedness of mind, included among the means of hiding one's own faults.

terms.root: √mad「陶醉」 · √mad "to be intoxicated"
terms.short_zh: 對自己的盛事深生染著，陶醉傲慢；以貪為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Haughtiness — deep attachment to one's own good fortune, intoxicated and proud; a part of greed.
terms.detail_zh:
mada 原義是「醉」。《成唯識論》：「於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性；能障不憍，染依為業。」「盛事」指自己的財富、容貌、才能、家世、健康、年輕等；對這些陶醉而驕傲，就是憍。

體性：「此亦貪愛一分為體」——憍是對自身所有的貪著。與根本煩惱「慢」的區別：慢是和他人比較而高舉，憍不必比較，只是自我陶醉（見比較卡）。

《遺教經》：「憍慢尚非世俗白衣所宜，何況出家入道之人。」
terms.detail_en:
Mada originally means "intoxication". Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride; it obstructs non-haughtiness and is the basis of defilement." "Flourishing" means one's wealth, looks, talent, family, health, youth; being intoxicated with them is haughtiness.

Substance: "a part of greed" — attachment to what one has. Versus the root affliction pride: pride exalts oneself by comparison with others; haughtiness needs no comparison, just self-intoxication.

The Yijiao jing: "Arrogance is unfitting even for laypeople in the world, how much more for those who have left home to enter the path."

quotes.text: 云何為憍？於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性；能障不憍，染依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is haughtiness? Its nature is deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride; its function is to obstruct non-haughtiness and be the basis of defilement.

quotes.text: 云何為憍？謂於自盛事染著倨傲心恃為性。
quotes.note_en: What is haughtiness? Its nature is attachment to one's own flourishing, arrogant self-reliance.

quotes.text: 憍慢尚非世俗白衣所宜，何況出家入道之人
quotes.source_en: Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching (Yijiao jing)
quotes.note_en: Arrogance is unfitting even for laypeople in the world, how much more for those who have left home to enter the path.

terms.root: vi-√hiṃs「傷害」 · vi-√hiṃs "to injure"
terms.short_zh: 對有情心無悲愍而損惱之；以瞋為體。小隨煩惱之一，與不害相對。
terms.short_en: Harmfulness — lacking compassion and tormenting beings; a part of aversion. Opposite of non-harming.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於諸有情，心無悲愍，損惱為性；能障不害，逼惱為業。」害的核心是「**心無悲愍**」——看見眾生受苦不起同情，反而加以逼迫。

體性：「此亦瞋恚一分為體。」至於瞋與害的差別，論中說「瞋、害別相，准善應說」——比照無瞋與不害來理解：瞋障礙給樂的慈，害障礙拔苦的悲。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is tormenting beings, the mind lacking compassion; it obstructs non-harming and its function is oppression." Its core is **absence of compassion**: seeing beings suffer without sympathy, one adds to their torment.

Substance: "a part of aversion". As for how aversion and harmfulness differ, the treatise says "their distinct characteristics are to be understood by analogy with the wholesome" — i.e. with non-hatred and non-harming: aversion obstructs loving-kindness (giving happiness), harmfulness obstructs compassion (removing suffering).

quotes.text: 云何為害？於諸有情，心無悲愍，損惱為性；能障不害，逼惱為業。
quotes.note_en: What is harmfulness? Its nature is tormenting beings, the mind lacking compassion; its function is to obstruct non-harming and oppress.

quotes.text: 云何為害？謂於諸有情損惱為性。
quotes.note_en: What is harmfulness? Its nature is tormenting sentient beings.

terms.root: √īrṣy「嫉妒」 · √īrṣy "to envy"
terms.short_zh: 為自己的名利，不能忍受他人榮盛而妒忌，內心憂戚；以瞋為體。小隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Jealousy — for the sake of one's own fame and gain, being unable to bear others' success; it brings sorrow. A part of aversion.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「徇自名利，不耐他榮，妬忌為性；能障不嫉，憂慼為業。」嫉是看到別人比自己好（榮盛）就受不了。「憂慼為業」：嫉妒的人見他人得意，自己便悶悶不樂。

體性是「瞋恚一分」——對他人的好事起憎。它與隨喜（muditā，四無量心之「喜」）正好相反。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Pursuing one's own fame and gain, unable to bear others' glory, its nature is envy; it obstructs non-jealousy and its function is sorrow." Seeing others doing well is intolerable; seeing their success, the jealous grow gloomy.

Its substance is a part of aversion — hostility toward others' good fortune. It is the exact opposite of sympathetic joy (muditā, the third immeasurable).

quotes.text: 云何為嫉？徇自名利，不耐他榮，妬忌為性；能障不嫉，憂慼為業。
quotes.note_en: What is jealousy? Pursuing one's own fame and gain, unable to bear others' glory, its nature is envy; its function is to obstruct non-jealousy and cause sorrow.

quotes.text: 云何為嫉？謂於他盛事心妬為性。
quotes.note_en: What is jealousy? Its nature is the mind's envy at others' flourishing.

terms.root: matsara「吝嗇、妒」 · matsara "selfish, envious"
terms.short_zh: 耽著財物與佛法，不肯惠施，祕藏吝惜；以貪為體。小隨煩惱之一，與布施相違。
terms.short_en: Stinginess — clinging to wealth and Dharma, unwilling to give, secretive and grudging; a part of greed. Opposed to generosity.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「耽著財、法，不能慧捨，祕悋為性；能障不慳，鄙畜為業。」慳的對象不只財物，也包括「法」——知道了佛法卻捨不得教人，也是慳。「鄙畜為業」：吝嗇的人連無用之物也鄙陋地囤積。

體性：「此即貪愛一分為體。」慳與布施（dāna）相違——《大乘五蘊論》直說：「施相違心悋為性。」
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Clinging to wealth and Dharma, unable to give wisely, its nature is secretive grudging; it obstructs non-stinginess and its function is mean hoarding." Its object includes not only wealth but also **Dharma** — knowing the teaching yet begrudging it to others is also stinginess.

Substance: "a part of greed". It opposes generosity (dāna); the Pañcaskandhaka simply says: "its nature is grudging, contrary to giving."

quotes.text: 云何為慳？耽著財、法，不能慧捨，祕悋為性；能障不慳，鄙畜為業。
quotes.note_en: What is stinginess? Clinging to wealth and Dharma, unable to give them away wisely, its nature is secretive grudging; its function is to obstruct non-stinginess and cause mean hoarding.

quotes.text: 云何為慳？謂施相違心悋為性。
quotes.note_en: What is stinginess? Its nature is grudging, contrary to giving.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ hrī「慚」 · a- + hrī "shame"
terms.short_zh: 不顧自身與正法，輕拒賢善；與一切不善心俱起。中隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Lack of self-respect — disregarding oneself and the Dharma, rejecting the good; present in every unwholesome mind.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「不顧自、法，輕拒賢善為性；能障礙慚，生長惡行為業。」正是「慚」的反面：不顧自己的人格、不顧正法，對賢善之人事輕視拒斥。

無慚與無愧是**中隨煩惱**：凡是不善心都一定有它們（遍不善），但在有覆無記心中則無。《成唯識論》判定它們「定是實有」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Disregarding oneself and the Dharma, its nature is disdaining and rejecting the worthy and good; it obstructs self-respect and causes misconduct to grow" — the exact reverse of hrī.

With lack of decorum it forms the **intermediate secondary afflictions**: present in every unwholesome mind, but not in obscured-neutral minds. The Cheng weishi lun rules that both "are definitely real".

quotes.text: 云何無慚？不顧自、法，輕拒賢善為性；能障礙慚，生長惡行為業。
quotes.note_en: What is lack of self-respect? Disregarding oneself and the Dharma, its nature is disdaining and rejecting the worthy and good; its function is to obstruct self-respect and make misconduct grow.

quotes.text: 云何無慚？謂於所作罪不自羞恥為性。
quotes.note_en: What is lack of self-respect? Its nature is not feeling ashamed within oneself of the wrong one has done.

terms.root: an-「非」＋ apatrāpya「愧」 · an- + apatrāpya "decorum"
terms.short_zh: 不顧世間譏評，崇重暴惡；與一切不善心俱起。中隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Lack of decorum — disregarding the world's censure and honouring the violent and evil; present in every unwholesome mind.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「不顧世間，崇重暴惡為性；能障礙愧，生長惡行為業。」這是「愧」的反面：不在乎別人怎麼看，甚至推崇暴惡。

論中特別辨明：無慚、無愧雖都以「不羞恥過惡」為共相，但無慚是「不顧自、法」，無愧是「不顧世間」，所以是兩個不同的心所。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Disregarding the world, its nature is honouring the violent and evil; it obstructs decorum and causes misconduct to grow" — the reverse of apatrāpya: not caring what others think, even admiring violence.

The treatise stresses that although both share "no shame at wrongdoing", lack of self-respect disregards oneself and the Dharma, lack of decorum disregards the world; hence they are two distinct factors.

quotes.text: 云何無愧？不顧世間，崇重暴惡為性；能障礙愧，生長惡行為業。
quotes.note_en: What is lack of decorum? Disregarding the world, its nature is honouring the violent and evil; its function is to obstruct decorum and make misconduct grow.

quotes.text: 云何無愧？謂於所作罪不羞恥他為性。
quotes.note_en: What is lack of decorum? Its nature is not feeling ashamed before others of the wrong one has done.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ śraddhā「信」 · a- + śraddhā "faith"
terms.short_zh: 對實、德、能不忍樂欲，心地穢濁；懶惰的所依。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Lack of faith — not accepting or delighting in the real, the virtuous and the capable; a turbid mind, the basis of laziness.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於實、德、能不忍樂欲，心穢為性；能障淨信，惰依為業。」恰與信（心淨）相反：不信「自相渾濁，復能渾濁餘心、心所，如極穢物，自穢、穢他」。

「惰依為業」：不相信修行有用、不相信自己做得到，自然就懶於修善——所以不信是懈怠的所依。它是遍一切染心的大隨煩惱，「定是實有」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is non-acceptance, non-delight and non-aspiration toward the real, the virtuous and the capable, with turbidity of mind; it obstructs pure faith and is the basis of laziness." It mirrors faith (clarity): faithlessness "is turbid in itself and makes other minds and factors turbid, like filth that soils itself and others."

"Basis of laziness": not believing practice works or that one can succeed, one naturally neglects the good. It is a major secondary affliction present in every defiled mind, and "definitely real".

quotes.text: 云何不信？於實、德、能不忍樂欲，心穢為性；能障淨信，惰依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is lack of faith? Its nature is non-acceptance, non-delight and non-aspiration toward the real, the virtuous and the capable, with turbidity of mind; its function is to obstruct pure faith and be the basis of laziness.

quotes.text: 唯此不信，自相渾濁，復能渾濁餘心、心所，如極穢物，自穢、穢他
quotes.note_en: This lack of faith alone is turbid in its own character and also makes other minds and mental factors turbid, like filthy matter that soils itself and soils others.

terms.root: kusīda「懶惰的」 · from kusīda "lazy"
terms.short_zh: 在修善斷惡上懶惰；障礙精進，增長雜染。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Laziness — sluggishness in cultivating good and abandoning evil; obstructs diligence and increases defilement.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於善、惡品修、斷事中，懶惰為性；能障精進，增染為業。」懈怠專指在**修善、斷惡**上的懶惰。

有意思的是：熱衷於惡事、勤於無記之事，並不算「不懈怠」。論中說：「於諸染事而策勤者，亦名懈怠，退善法故。」——忙碌於錯誤的事，本身就是對善法的怠惰。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is sluggishness in cultivating the good and abandoning the bad; it obstructs diligence and increases defilement." Kausīdya refers specifically to laziness about **cultivating good and abandoning evil**.

Interestingly, zeal for harmful things does not count as its opposite: the treatise says that exerting oneself in defiled affairs "is also called laziness, because it causes the good to decline" — being busy with the wrong things is itself neglect of the good.

quotes.text: 云何懈怠？於善、惡品修、斷事中，懶惰為性；能障精進，增染為業。
quotes.note_en: What is laziness? Its nature is sluggishness in cultivating the good and abandoning the bad; its function is to obstruct diligence and increase defilement.

quotes.text: 云何懈怠？謂精進所治，於諸善品心不勇猛為性。
quotes.note_en: What is laziness? As what diligence counteracts, its nature is the mind's lack of vigour toward wholesome things.

terms.root: pra-√mad「沉醉、疏忽」 · pra-√mad "to be careless, intoxicated"
terms.short_zh: 於染淨品不能防惡修善而縱蕩；由懈怠與貪瞋癡假立。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Heedlessness — failing to guard against evil and cultivate good, letting oneself go; designated on laziness and the three poisons.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於染、淨品，不能防、修，縱蕩為性；障不放逸，增惡損善所依為業。」論中說明：「謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡，不能防修染淨品法，總名放逸，非別有體。」

這與「不放逸」恰成對稱：不放逸以精進與三善根假立，放逸則以懈怠與三不善根假立。佛陀最後的教誨「無為放逸」，所針對的就是它。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is letting oneself go, unable to guard against the defiled or cultivate the pure; it obstructs conscientiousness and is the basis for increasing evil and diminishing good." It explains: "Laziness and greed, hatred and delusion, being unable to guard against the defiled and cultivate the pure, are collectively called heedlessness; it has no separate entity."

This mirrors conscientiousness exactly: conscientiousness is designated on diligence plus the three wholesome roots, heedlessness on laziness plus the three unwholesome roots. The Buddha's last words, "do not be heedless", target it.

quotes.text: 云何放逸？於染、淨品，不能防、修，縱蕩為性；障不放逸，增惡損善所依為業。謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡，不能防修染淨品法，總名放逸，非別有體。
quotes.note_en: What is heedlessness? Its nature is letting oneself go, unable to guard against the defiled or cultivate the pure; its function is to obstruct conscientiousness and be the basis for increasing evil and diminishing good. That is, laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion, being unable to guard against and cultivate defiled and pure dharmas, is collectively called heedlessness; it has no separate substance.

quotes.text: 云何放逸？謂即由貪瞋癡懈怠故，於諸煩惱心不防護，於諸善品不能修習為性。
quotes.note_en: What is heedlessness? Because of greed, hatred, delusion and laziness, its nature is not guarding the mind against afflictions and being unable to cultivate the good.

terms.root: √styai「凝結、變硬」 · √styai "to congeal, stiffen"
terms.short_zh: 令心於境昏昧沉重、無所堪任；障礙輕安與觀。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Torpor — mind dull and heavy, unfit for its object; obstructs pliancy and insight (vipaśyanā).
terms.detail_zh:
styāna 原義是「凝結」——心像凝固了一樣沉重。《成唯識論》：「令心於境，無堪任為性；能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業。」

惛沈是禪修的兩大障礙之一：惛沈使心下沉、昏昧，障礙清明的「觀」（vipaśyanā）；另一個是掉舉，使心上浮、散動，障礙寂靜的「止」（śamatha）。對治惛沈的善心所是輕安。

惛沈與睡眠常合為「惛沈睡眠蓋」（五蓋之一），但兩者不同：惛沈是心的沉重無力，睡眠是心識昧略、身不自在（見比較卡）。
terms.detail_en:
Styāna originally means "congealing": the mind as if set solid, heavy. Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is making the mind unfit for its object; it obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā (insight)."

Torpor is one of the two great obstacles in meditation: it makes the mind sink and grow dim, obstructing clear insight; the other, restlessness, makes it float and scatter, obstructing calm (śamatha). Its wholesome antidote is pliancy.

With sleep it forms the hindrance "torpor and sleep", but they differ: torpor is heaviness and powerlessness of mind; sleep is a dim, contracted state in which the body is not under control (see the comparison card).

quotes.text: 云何惛沈？令心於境，無堪任為性；能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業。
quotes.note_en: What is torpor? Its nature is making the mind unfit with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct pliancy and vipaśyanā.

quotes.text: 云何惛沈？謂心不調暢無所堪能蒙昧為性。
quotes.note_en: What is torpor? Its nature is the mind being unfluent, unfit and dim.

terms.root: ud-√dhṛ「上揚、浮動」 · from ud-dhata "raised up, agitated"
terms.short_zh: 令心於境不寂靜，浮動上揚；障礙行捨與止。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Restlessness — the mind not calm on its object, bubbling up; obstructs equanimity and calm (śamatha).
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「令心於境不寂靜為性；能障行捨、奢摩他為業。」掉舉是心的「浮動」——念頭一個接一個冒上來，靜不下來。

論中記載一說：「掉舉貪一分攝……此由憶昔樂事生故」——常因回想過去快樂的事而起，所以與貪相關。對治它的是行捨；在禪修中，它障礙止（śamatha），與障礙觀的惛沈是一對。

掉舉與散亂的差別：掉舉令心「不寂靜」（一個對象上浮動不安），散亂令心「流蕩」（在不同對象間跳躍）。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is making the mind not calm with regard to its object; it obstructs equanimity and śamatha." Restlessness is the mind's "bubbling up": thoughts popping up one after another, unable to settle.

The treatise records the view that "restlessness is a part of greed … arising from recalling past pleasures". Its antidote is equanimity; in meditation it obstructs calm, pairing with torpor, which obstructs insight.

Restlessness versus distraction: restlessness makes the mind "not calm" (agitated even on one object); distraction makes it "drift" (jumping between objects).

quotes.text: 云何掉舉？令心於境不寂靜為性；能障行捨、奢摩他為業。
quotes.note_en: What is restlessness? Its nature is making the mind not calm with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct equanimity and śamatha.

quotes.text: 掉舉貪一分攝，論唯說此是貪分故，此由憶昔樂事生故。
quotes.note_en: One view: restlessness belongs to a part of greed, since the treatises only call it a part of greed; it arises from recalling past pleasures.

terms.root: muṣita「被偷走的」＋ smṛti「念」 · muṣita "stolen" + smṛti "mindfulness"
terms.short_zh: 對所緣不能明記，正念被「偷走」；散亂的所依。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Forgetfulness — unable to keep objects clearly in mind, mindfulness "stolen"; the basis of distraction.
terms.detail_zh:
梵語直譯「被偷走的念」。《成唯識論》：「於諸所緣，不能明記為性；能障正念、散亂所依為業。」失念使人忘失應當專注的對象，心便隨之散亂。

體性：論中有三說——「念一分」（與煩惱相應的念）、「癡一分」、以及「俱一分攝」（念與癡各一分）。《成唯識論》判定大隨中的放逸、失念、不正知三者「定是假有」。《大乘五蘊論》說它是「染污念」。
terms.detail_en:
Literally "stolen mindfulness". Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is being unable to remember objects clearly; it obstructs right mindfulness and is the basis of distraction." Losing the object one should hold, the mind scatters.

Substance: the treatise gives three views — a part of mindfulness (mindfulness bound up with afflictions), a part of delusion, or a part of both. It rules that heedlessness, forgetfulness and non-alertness among the major secondary afflictions are "definitely designated". The Pañcaskandhaka calls it "defiled mindfulness".

quotes.text: 云何失念？於諸所緣，不能明記為性；能障正念、散亂所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is forgetfulness? Its nature is being unable to remember objects clearly; its function is to obstruct right mindfulness and be the basis of distraction.

quotes.text: 云何失念？謂染污念，於諸善法不能明記為性。
quotes.note_en: What is forgetfulness? It is defiled mindfulness; its nature is being unable to remember wholesome dharmas clearly.

terms.root: vi-√kṣip「拋散」 · vi-√kṣip "to throw about, scatter"
terms.short_zh: 令心在諸所緣間流蕩；障礙正定，是惡慧的所依。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Distraction — the mind drifting among objects; obstructs right concentration and is the basis of wrong discernment.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於諸所緣，令心流蕩為性；能障正定，惡慧所依為業。」散亂是心從一個對象跳到另一個對象，無法定住。

**散亂與掉舉**：論中問「掉舉、散亂二用何別？」答：「彼令易解，此令易緣」——掉舉令心頻頻變換理解、浮動不安；散亂令心頻頻轉換對象。

**散亂與失念**：失念是忘失所緣，散亂是隨後心的流蕩——失念為「散亂所依」。《大乘五蘊論》：「貪瞋癡分心流蕩為性。」
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is making the mind drift among objects; it obstructs right concentration and is the basis of wrong discernment." Distraction is jumping from object to object, unable to settle.

**Distraction vs restlessness**: the treatise asks how their functions differ and answers: "the former makes [the mind] change its understanding, the latter makes it change its object" — restlessness is agitation in how one apprehends, distraction is switching objects.

**Distraction vs forgetfulness**: forgetfulness loses the object, distraction is the drifting that follows — forgetfulness is "the basis of distraction". Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is the drifting of mind, part of greed, hatred and delusion."

quotes.text: 云何散亂？於諸所緣，令心流蕩為性；能障正定，惡慧所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is distraction? Its nature is making the mind drift among objects; its function is to obstruct right concentration and be the basis of wrong discernment.

quotes.text: 掉舉、散亂二用何別？彼令易解，此令易緣
quotes.note_en: How do restlessness and distraction differ in function? The former makes [the mind] change its understanding; the latter makes it change its object.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ saṃprajanya「正知」 · a- + saṃprajanya "clear comprehension"
terms.short_zh: 對所觀境錯誤理解，不清楚自己在做什麼；導致毀犯。大隨煩惱之一。
terms.short_en: Non-alertness — misunderstanding what is observed, not clearly knowing what one is doing; leads to transgression.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於所觀境，謬解為性；能障正知、毀犯為業。」正知（saṃprajanya）是對自己身、語、意當下行為的清楚覺察；不正知則是覺察錯誤或缺失，因而做出違犯戒律的事。《大乘五蘊論》：「於身語意現前行中不正依住為性。」

體性：一說「慧一分」（與煩惱相應的慧），一說「癡一分」，一說兩者「俱一分攝」；判為「定是假有」。與「惡見」同為染慧的一種表現，但惡見是對諦理的錯誤推度，不正知是對當下行為的錯誤覺知。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is misunderstanding the observed object; it obstructs right awareness and its function is transgression." Clear comprehension is lucid awareness of one's present bodily, verbal and mental conduct; non-alertness is faulty or absent awareness, so one commits transgressions. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is not abiding correctly in present conduct of body, speech and mind."

Substance: a part of discernment (discernment bound up with afflictions), a part of delusion, or a part of both; it is "definitely designated". Like wrong view it is a form of defiled discernment, but wrong view misjudges the truths, non-alertness misreads one's present conduct.

quotes.text: 云何不正知？於所觀境，謬解為性；能障正知、毀犯為業。
quotes.note_en: What is non-alertness? Its nature is misunderstanding the observed object; its function is to obstruct right awareness and cause transgression.

quotes.text: 云何不正知？謂於身語意現前行中不正依住為性。
quotes.note_en: What is non-alertness? Its nature is not abiding correctly in present conduct of body, speech and mind.

terms.root: ku-kṛta「做壞了的事」 · from ku-kṛta "badly done"
terms.short_zh: 對已做（或未做）之事追悔；障礙止。不定心所：悔惡是善，悔善是惡。
terms.short_en: Regret — remorse over what one did (or failed to do); obstructs calm. Indeterminate: regretting evil is good, regretting good is bad.
terms.detail_zh:
kaukṛtya 字面是「做壞了的事」，漢譯「惡作」，又稱「悔」。《成唯識論》：「悔謂惡作，惡所作業，追悔為性，障止為業。」論中解釋：這是「於果假立因名」——追悔（果）以所厭惡的作業（因）為名；而且後悔「先前沒做」的事也算惡作。

**為什麼是「不定」**：悔本身的善惡取決於所悔之事——後悔做了壞事是善的（懺悔），後悔做了好事則是不善。追悔太過則令心不安，障礙止（śamatha）；掉舉與惡作合為五蓋之一「掉悔蓋」。
terms.detail_en:
Kaukṛtya literally means "what was badly done"; Chinese 惡作 or 悔 "regret". Cheng weishi lun: "Regret is 'evil-doing': its nature is remorse over a disliked deed; its function is to obstruct calm." The name "applies the cause's name to the effect" — the remorse (effect) is named after the deed regretted (cause); and regretting what one failed to do also counts.

**Why indeterminate**: its moral quality depends on what is regretted — regretting wrongdoing is wholesome (repentance), regretting a good deed is unwholesome. Excessive remorse disturbs the mind and obstructs calm; with restlessness it forms the hindrance "restlessness and remorse".

quotes.text: 悔謂惡作，惡所作業，追悔為性，障止為業。
quotes.note_en: Regret is "evil-doing": its nature is remorse over a disliked deed; its function is to obstruct calm.

quotes.text: 云何惡作？謂心變悔為性。
quotes.note_en: What is regret? Its nature is the mind's changing to remorse.

terms.root: 「昏睡、遲鈍」 · "sleepiness, sluggishness"
terms.short_zh: 令身不自在、心極闇昧的狀態；障礙觀。不定心所。
terms.short_en: Sleep — a state in which the body is not under control and the mind very dim and contracted; obstructs insight. Indeterminate.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「眠謂睡眠，令身不自在，昧、略為性，障觀為業。」論中解釋：「昧」簡別於定（定中心明而非昧），「略」簡別於醒時（醒時心識廣而不略）。睡眠位中身不自在、「心極闇劣，一門轉故」。

睡眠是心所而非單純的生理現象，所以通善、惡、無記：例如睡前的善念可延續到睡中。它與惛沈合為「惛沈睡眠蓋」，但惛沈是遍一切染心的大隨煩惱，睡眠則是不定。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Sleep makes the body not under one's control; its nature is dimness and contraction; its function is to obstruct insight." "Dim" distinguishes it from concentration (the concentrated mind is clear); "contracted" distinguishes it from waking. In sleep the body is not free and "the mind is extremely dark and weak, operating through a single door".

Sleep is a mental factor, not just physiology, so it can be wholesome, unwholesome or neutral — e.g. a good intention before sleep can carry into it. With torpor it forms the hindrance "torpor and sleep", but torpor is a major secondary affliction present in all defiled minds, whereas sleep is indeterminate.

quotes.text: 眠謂睡眠，令身不自在，昧、略為性，障觀為業。
quotes.note_en: Sleep makes the body not under one's control; its nature is dimness and contraction; its function is to obstruct insight.

quotes.text: 云何睡眠？謂不自在轉心極昧略為性。
quotes.note_en: What is sleep? Its nature is the mind operating without control, extremely dim and contracted.

terms.root: vi-√tark「推想、思量」 · vi-√tark "to reflect, conjecture"
terms.short_zh: 對意言境粗略地尋求推度；與伺相對（伺較細）。不定心所。舊譯「覺」。
terms.short_en: Initial inquiry — coarse searching of the mentally-verbalized object; contrasted with the finer vicāra. Indeterminate. Old translation 覺.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「尋謂尋求，令心怱遽於意言境，麁轉為性；伺謂伺察，令心怱遽於意言境，細轉為性。此二俱以安、不安住身心分位所依為業。」

「意言境」指以內在語言、概念所把握的對象。尋是較粗的「搜尋」，伺是較細的「審察」。二者都以思（意志）與慧（簡擇）為體，在推度的深淺上分別。

**禪定中的意義**：初禪有尋有伺，二禪以上無尋無伺——尋伺的止息是從初禪進入二禪的關鍵。說一切有部以「心麁性名尋，心細性名伺」簡要說明。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Initial inquiry means searching: making the mind hurried toward the mentally-verbalized object, operating coarsely; sustained investigation means scrutinizing: … operating finely. Both serve as the basis of bodily and mental states of ease or unease."

The "mentally-verbalized object" is what is grasped through inner speech and concepts. Vitarka is the coarser "searching", vicāra the finer "examining". Both have volition and discernment as substance, differing in depth.

**In meditation**: the first dhyāna has vitarka and vicāra; the second and higher have neither — their cessation marks the move to the second dhyāna. The Sarvāstivāda sums it up: "coarseness of mind is vitarka, fineness of mind is vicāra."

quotes.text: 尋謂尋求，令心怱遽於意言境，麁轉為性；伺謂伺察，令心怱遽於意言境，細轉為性。此二俱以安、不安住身心分位所依為業。
quotes.note_en: Initial inquiry means searching — making the mind hurry toward the mentally-verbalized object, its nature operating coarsely; sustained investigation means scrutinizing — making the mind hurry toward the mentally-verbalized object, its nature operating finely. Both function as the basis of bodily and mental states of ease or unease.

quotes.text: 云何為尋？謂能尋求意言分別思慧差別令心麁為性。
quotes.note_en: What is initial inquiry? Its nature is searching the mental discourse, a particular kind of volition and discernment, making the mind coarse.

quotes.text: 心麁性名尋。心細性名伺。
quotes.note_en: Coarseness of mind is called initial inquiry; fineness of mind is called sustained investigation.

terms.root: vi-√car「往來巡察」 · vi-√car "to move about, examine"
terms.short_zh: 對意言境細密地伺察；與尋相對（尋較粗）。不定心所。舊譯「觀」。
terms.short_en: Sustained investigation — fine scrutiny of the mentally-verbalized object; contrasted with the coarser vitarka. Indeterminate. Old translation 觀.
terms.detail_zh:
伺是細密的審察：尋像是在人群中「找」一個人，伺則是找到之後「仔細端詳」。《大乘五蘊論》：「謂能伺察意言分別思慧差別令心細為性。」

**名稱陷阱**：舊譯把 vitarka、vicāra 譯為「覺、觀」，這個「觀」和止觀的「觀」（vipaśyanā）是完全不同的字！讀古譯經典（如「有覺有觀三昧」）時要特別注意。
terms.detail_en:
Vicāra is fine scrutiny: vitarka is like "looking for" someone in a crowd, vicāra like "examining them closely" once found. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is scrutinizing the mental discourse, a particular kind of volition and discernment, making the mind fine."

**Naming trap**: older translations render vitarka and vicāra as 覺 and 觀 — this 觀 is entirely different from the 觀 of 止觀 (vipaśyanā)! Watch for it in old translations such as 「有覺有觀三昧」.

quotes.text: 云何為伺？謂能伺察意言分別思慧差別令心細為性。
quotes.note_en: What is sustained investigation? Its nature is scrutinizing the mental discourse, a particular kind of volition and discernment, making the mind fine.

terms.root: √chand「喜好、欲求」 · √chand "to please, to wish"
terms.short_zh: 對所樂之境的希望、意欲；精進的所依。別境心所之一，本身通善、惡、無記。
terms.short_en: Aspiration — wishing for a desired object; the support of effort. An object-specific factor, itself morally neutral.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於所樂境，希望為性，勤依為業。」欲是「想要」的心理動力；「勤依為業」說明它是精進的所依——想要成就善法，才會努力。

**欲不等於貪**。欲本身是中性的：希求善法的是「善法欲」，如求解脫、求菩提之心；對五欲境的染著希求才與貪（rāga）相應。所以佛典說「斷貪」，卻不說「斷欲」一概而論。

**學派差異**：說一切有部把欲列為「大地法」（每一念心都有）；唯識學則認為欲只在面對「所樂境」時生起，並非遍一切心，故移入「別境」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is wishing for a desired object; its function is to be the support of effort." Chanda is the motivational pull of "wanting to"; being "the support of effort" means one strives only for what one wishes to attain.

**Chanda is not greed.** In itself it is neutral: wishing for the good (dharma-chanda, e.g. aspiring to liberation) is wholesome; only defiled longing for sense objects goes with greed (rāga). So one is told to abandon greed, not every kind of wish.

**School difference**: the Sarvāstivāda counts chanda among the universal factors (in every mind); Yogācāra holds that it arises only toward a desired object, so it is object-specific.

quotes.text: 云何為欲？於所樂境，希望為性，勤依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is aspiration? Its nature is wishing for a desired object; its function is to serve as the support of effort.

quotes.text: 云何為欲？謂於可愛事，希望為性。
quotes.note_en: What is aspiration? Its nature is wishing for an attractive thing.

terms.root: adhi-√muc「確定、決斷」 · adhi-√muc "to be set upon, decide"
terms.short_zh: 對已確定的對象加以印可、堅持，不被他說動搖。別境心所之一。
terms.short_en: Resolve — confirming and holding firmly to what has been ascertained, so that one cannot be swayed. An object-specific factor.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於決定境，印持為性，不可引轉為業。」勝解是對已確認之事「蓋章認定」的作用：一旦印持，就不被其他說法牽引改變。

勝解只在「決定境」上生起——若猶豫不決（疑），就沒有勝解。它本身通善惡：對正理的勝解是善，對邪說的堅定認定則是「邪勝解」。

**與信的分別**：勝解是認知上的「確定」；信（śraddhā）則以「心淨」為性，含有對實、德、能的信樂。詳見比較卡「勝解與信」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is confirming and holding to an ascertained object; its function is that one cannot be turned away." Adhimokṣa is the mind's "seal of approval" on what it has settled: once confirmed, other views cannot drag it away.

It arises only toward an ascertained object — where there is hesitation (doubt), there is no resolve. It is morally variable: firm conviction in the truth is wholesome, firm conviction in a false teaching is "wrong resolve".

**Versus faith**: resolve is cognitive certainty; faith (śraddhā) has clarity of mind as its nature and includes trust and delight. See the comparison card.

quotes.text: 云何勝解？於決定境，印持為性，不可引轉為業。
quotes.note_en: What is resolve? Its nature is confirming and holding to an ascertained object; its function is that it cannot be drawn away.

quotes.text: 云何勝解？謂於決定事，即如所了印可為性。
quotes.note_en: What is resolve? With regard to an ascertained thing, its nature is to affirm it just as it has been understood.

terms.root: √smṛ「記憶」 · √smṛ "to remember"
terms.short_zh: 對曾經歷之境明記不忘；定的所依。別境心所之一，修行中的「正念」即其善的一面。
terms.short_en: Mindfulness — clearly keeping in mind what has been experienced, without forgetting; the support of concentration.
terms.detail_zh:
smṛti 本義是「記憶」。《成唯識論》：「於曾習境，令心明記不忘為性，定依為業。」念使心持續地「記住」所緣，不讓它滑失，所以是定的基礎。

**念的範圍**：唯識學認為念只緣「曾習境」（熟悉過的對象），對全新的對象不起念，故屬別境；說一切有部則列為大地法。

**正念與失念**：《成唯識論》說「不忘念者，即是正念」。與煩惱相應、令人忘失正所緣的，則是隨煩惱中的「失念」。四念處（smṛtyupasthāna）、八正道的「正念」，都是念的修習。
terms.detail_en:
Smṛti originally means "memory". Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is to make the mind clearly remember a familiar object without forgetting; its function is to be the support of concentration." Mindfulness keeps the object "in mind" so it does not slip away — the basis of samādhi.

**Scope**: Yogācāra holds that mindfulness takes only a "previously experienced" object, so it is object-specific; the Sarvāstivāda counts it as universal.

**Right mindfulness and forgetfulness**: the Cheng weishi lun says "non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness". Mindfulness bound up with afflictions, losing the proper object, is the secondary affliction "forgetfulness" (muṣitasmṛtitā). The four foundations of mindfulness and the "right mindfulness" of the eightfold path are its cultivation.

quotes.text: 云何為念？於曾習境，令心明記不忘為性，定依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is mindfulness? Its nature is to make the mind clearly remember a familiar object without forgetting; its function is to serve as the support of concentration.

quotes.text: 云何為念？謂於串習事，令心不忘明記為性。
quotes.note_en: What is mindfulness? With regard to a habitually familiar thing, its nature is to keep the mind from forgetting and to remember clearly.

quotes.text: 不忘念者，即是正念。
quotes.note_en: Non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness.

terms.root: sam-ā-√dhā「置於一處、聚合」 · sam-ā-√dhā "to put together, collect"
terms.short_zh: 令心專注於所觀境而不散亂；智慧的所依。別境心所之一，也是三學之一。
terms.short_en: Concentration — keeping the mind focused on its object without scattering; the support of wisdom.
terms.detail_zh:
音譯「三摩地、三昧」，意譯「等持」（平等持心）。《成唯識論》：「於所觀境，令心專注不散為性，智依為業。」定使心穩定於一境，由此產生觀察的智慧（「智依」）。《大乘五蘊論》：「令心一境不散為性。」

**作為心所**的定，是任何「專注觀察」時都有的作用；**作為修行**，則是戒、定、慧三學之一，八正道的「正定」，以及種種禪定（dhyāna）、等至（samāpatti）的共同核心。

唯識學認為定只在「所觀境」上生起，散亂心中沒有，故列別境；說一切有部列為大地法（稱三摩地）。
terms.detail_en:
Transliterated 三摩地/三昧, translated 等持 "even holding". Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is to make the mind focus on the observed object without scattering; its function is to be the support of wisdom." Stability on one object makes discerning insight possible. Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is to keep the mind on one object, undistracted."

**As a mental factor**, samādhi is present whenever the mind attends closely to what it observes; **as a practice**, it is the second of the three trainings (morality, concentration, wisdom), the "right concentration" of the eightfold path, and the common core of the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) and attainments (samāpatti).

Yogācāra places it among the object-specific factors, since a scattered mind lacks it; the Sarvāstivāda counts it as universal.

quotes.text: 云何為定？於所觀境，令心專注不散為性，智依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is concentration? Its nature is to make the mind focus on the observed object without scattering; its function is to serve as the support of wisdom.

quotes.text: 云何三摩地？謂於所觀事，令心一境不散為性。
quotes.note_en: What is samādhi? With regard to the observed thing, its nature is to keep the mind on one object, undistracted.

terms.root: pra-√jñā「徹底地知」 · pra-√jñā "to know thoroughly"
terms.short_zh: 對所觀境的簡擇、分辨；能斷疑。作為心所通善惡，作為般若則是成佛的智慧。
terms.short_en: Wisdom/discernment — discriminating the observed object; it cuts off doubt. As a factor it can be wholesome or defiled; as prajñā-pāramitā it is liberating wisdom.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於所觀境，簡擇為性，斷疑為業。」慧是分辨是非、得失、真偽的作用；有了清楚的簡擇，疑惑自然斷除。

**慧本身通善惡**。《大乘五蘊論》說慧「或如理所引，或不如理所引，或俱非所引」。如理思惟而生的是善慧；錯誤推度的「惡見」其實也是一種慧——「染慧」。所以百法中「慧」列在別境，而不是善心所。

**般若**：六度中的般若波羅蜜（prajñā-pāramitā）、三學中的慧學，指的是如理、清淨、能斷煩惱的慧；漢譯保留音譯「般若」，以別於世間聰明。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is discriminating the observed object; its function is cutting off doubt." Prajñā sorts right from wrong, true from false; once things are clearly discerned, doubt ends.

**As a factor, prajñā can be defiled.** The Pañcaskandhaka says it may be "induced by proper reasoning, by improper reasoning, or by neither". Wisdom born of sound reflection is wholesome; the "wrong view" of the root afflictions is itself a kind of prajñā — "defiled discernment". That is why 慧 is an object-specific factor, not a wholesome one.

**Prajñā-pāramitā**: in the six perfections and the three trainings, prajñā means discernment that accords with reality, is pure, and cuts off afflictions; Chinese keeps the transliteration 般若 to set it apart from worldly cleverness.

quotes.text: 云何為慧？於所觀境，簡擇為性，斷疑為業。
quotes.note_en: What is wisdom? Its nature is discriminating the observed object; its function is cutting off doubt.

quotes.text: 云何為慧？謂即於彼擇法為性；或如理所引，或不如理所引，或俱非所引。
quotes.note_en: What is wisdom? Its nature is discerning dharmas with regard to that same [object]; it may be induced by proper reasoning, by improper reasoning, or by neither.

quotes.text: 佛法大海，信為能入，智為能度。
quotes.note_en: The great ocean of the Buddha's Dharma is entered by faith and crossed by wisdom.

terms.root: śrad-√dhā「置心於…、信賴」 · śrad-√dhā "to put one's heart on, trust"
terms.short_zh: 對實（真理）、德（三寶）、能（自己能成就）深忍樂欲，令心清淨。善心所之首。
terms.short_en: Faith — deep acceptance of, delight in and aspiration toward what is real, virtuous and attainable, making the mind clear. First of the wholesome factors.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲，心淨為性；對治不信，樂善為業。」論中把信的對象分為三：

1. **信實有**：於諸法實事理深信忍可（如業果、四諦）；
2. **信有德**：於三寶真淨功德深信愛樂；
3. **信有能**：於一切世、出世善，深信自己有能力得、能成就，而起希望。

「心淨為性」是信的關鍵：信像能澄清濁水的寶珠，不但自身清淨，也令其他心、心所清淨。與不信的「心穢」正好相反。佛教的信不是盲信，而是建立在「實、德、能」上的澄淨信任。

quotes.text: 云何為信？於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲，心淨為性；對治不信，樂善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is faith? Its nature is deep acceptance, delight and aspiration toward the real, the virtuous and the capable, with clarity of mind; its function is to counteract faithlessness and delight in the good.

quotes.text: 信為道元功德母，長養一切諸善法
quotes.note_en: Faith is the source of the Path and the mother of merit; it nourishes all good dharmas.

quotes.text: 佛法大海，信為能入，智為能度。
quotes.note_en: The great ocean of the Buddha's Dharma is entered by faith and crossed by wisdom.

terms.root: vīra「勇士」→「勇猛」 · from vīra "hero": heroism, vigour
terms.short_zh: 在修善、斷惡上勇猛而精純地努力；對治懈怠。善心所之一，也是六度之一。
terms.short_en: Diligence — courageous, unalloyed effort in cultivating good and abandoning evil; counteracts laziness.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「勤謂精進，於善、惡品修、斷事中，勇、悍為性；對治懈怠，滿善為業。」論中解釋：「勇」表示勝進，「悍」表示精純——不雜染污。

**不是所有努力都是精進**。為惡事或無記事而勤勞，不屬精進；只有在「修善」與「斷惡」上的努力才是。

精進也是六度（vīrya-pāramitā）、五根五力、七覺支與八正道（正精進）的一支。《遺教經》：「若勤精進，則事無難……譬如小水常流，則能穿石。」
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Diligence is courage and purity in the work of cultivating the good and abandoning the bad; it counteracts laziness and fulfils the good." "Courage" means advancing; "purity" means unmixed with defilement.

**Not all effort is diligence.** Working hard at harmful or merely neutral things is not vīrya; only effort in cultivating good and abandoning evil counts.

Vīrya is also one of the six perfections, the five faculties and powers, the seven factors of awakening and the eightfold path (right effort). The Yijiao jing: "If you are diligent, nothing is difficult … as a small stream flowing constantly can wear through stone."

quotes.text: 勤謂精進，於善、惡品修、斷事中，勇、悍為性；對治懈怠，滿善為業。
quotes.note_en: Effort means diligence: in cultivating the wholesome and abandoning the unwholesome, its nature is courage and purity; its function is to counteract laziness and fulfil the good.

quotes.text: 若勤精進則事無難者，是故汝等當勤精進，譬如小水常流則能穿石。
quotes.source_en: Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching (Yijiao jing)
quotes.note_en: If you are diligent, nothing is difficult. Therefore you should all be diligent — just as a small stream, flowing constantly, can wear through stone.

terms.root: √hrī「羞愧」 · √hrī "to be ashamed"
terms.short_zh: 依自身與正法的力量，尊重賢善、羞恥過惡；對治無慚。
terms.short_en: Self-respect — out of regard for oneself and the Dharma, honouring the good and feeling shame at wrongdoing.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「依自、法力，崇重賢、善為性；對治無慚，止息惡行為業。」慚是**向內**的羞恥：因為尊重自己的人格與所學的正法，所以不願作惡。

慚與愧常並稱。《雜阿含經》說「有二淨法，能護世間」，就是慚與愧；若無此二法，人倫秩序便會崩壞。兩者的區別在於羞恥的來源：慚依「自」與「法」，愧依「世間」。詳見比較卡「慚與愧」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Relying on the power of oneself and the Dharma, its nature is honouring the worthy and the good; it counteracts shamelessness and stops wrongdoing." Hrī is **inward-facing** shame: because one respects one's own integrity and the Dharma one follows, one is unwilling to do wrong.

It is paired with apatrāpya. The Saṃyuktāgama calls the two "the pure dharmas that protect the world"; without them, human society would collapse. The difference lies in the source: hrī relies on oneself and the Dharma, apatrāpya on the world. See the comparison card.

quotes.text: 云何為慚？依自、法力，崇重賢、善為性；對治無慚，止息惡行為業。
quotes.note_en: What is self-respect? Relying on the power of oneself and the Dharma, its nature is honouring the worthy and the good; its function is to counteract shamelessness and stop wrongdoing.

quotes.text: 云何為慚？謂自增上，及法增上，於所作罪羞恥為性。
quotes.note_en: What is self-respect? Out of regard for oneself and regard for the Dharma, its nature is feeling shame at the wrong one has done.

quotes.text: 有二淨法，能護世間。何等為二？所謂慚、愧。
quotes.note_en: There are two pure dharmas that protect the world. What are the two? Namely, self-respect and decorum (hrī and apatrāpya).

terms.root: apa-√trap「羞於（他人）」 · apa-√trap "to be ashamed before others"
terms.short_zh: 依世間輿論的力量，輕拒暴惡、羞於作罪；對治無愧。
terms.short_en: Decorum — out of regard for the world's opinion, rejecting violence and evil and feeling ashamed to do wrong.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「依世間力，輕拒暴惡為性；對治無愧，止息惡行為業。」愧是**向外**的羞恥：顧及他人的譏評、社會的規範而不敢作惡。

《大乘五蘊論》把兩者說得很清楚：慚是「自增上及法增上，於所作罪羞恥」；愧是「世增上，於所作罪羞恥」。一個內省、一個顧外，兩者合起來才能穩固地止息惡行。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Relying on the power of the world, its nature is disdaining and rejecting the violent and evil; it counteracts lack of decorum and stops wrongdoing." Apatrāpya is **outward-facing** shame: regard for others' censure and social norms restrains one from wrongdoing.

The Pañcaskandhaka puts the contrast neatly: self-respect is shame at wrongdoing "out of regard for oneself and the Dharma"; decorum is shame at wrongdoing "out of regard for the world". One looks inward, the other outward; together they restrain misconduct firmly.

quotes.text: 云何為愧？依世間力，輕拒暴惡為性；對治無愧，止息惡行為業。
quotes.note_en: What is decorum? Relying on the power of the world, its nature is disdaining and rejecting the violent and evil; its function is to counteract lack of decorum and stop wrongdoing.

quotes.text: 云何為愧？謂世增上，於所作罪羞恥為性。
quotes.note_en: What is decorum? Out of regard for the world, its nature is feeling shame at the wrong one has done.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ lobha「貪」 · a- "not" + lobha "greed"
terms.short_zh: 對三有及其因（有、有具）不染著；對治貪。三善根之一。
terms.short_en: Non-greed — no attachment to existence and its causes; counteracts greed. One of the three wholesome roots.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於有、有具，無著為性；對治貪著，作善為業。」「有」指三界的果報身，「有具」指能生三有的因與資具。無貪不只是「不貪」的消極狀態，而是一個積極的善心所——對它們不起執著。

無貪、無瞋、無癡合稱**三善根**（kuśala-mūla），是一切善法的根本，分別對治三不善根（貪、瞋、癡）。《大乘五蘊論》說無貪「令深厭患無著為性」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is non-attachment to existence and the means of existence; it counteracts greed and produces good." "Existence" is the resultant existence in the three realms; "the means of existence" are its causes and supports. Non-greed is not merely the absence of greed but a positive wholesome factor of non-clinging.

Non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion are the **three wholesome roots**, the basis of all good, countering the three unwholesome roots. The Pañcaskandhaka: "its nature is deep disenchantment and non-attachment."

quotes.text: 云何無貪？於有、有具，無著為性；對治貪著，作善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is non-greed? Its nature is non-attachment to existence and the means of existence; its function is to counteract greed and produce good.

quotes.text: 云何無貪？謂貪對治，令深厭患無著為性。
quotes.note_en: What is non-greed? As the antidote to greed, its nature is deep disenchantment and non-attachment.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ dveṣa「瞋」 · a- "not" + dveṣa "hatred"
terms.short_zh: 對苦及苦因不起憎恚；以慈為性，對治瞋。三善根之一。
terms.short_en: Non-hatred — no hostility toward suffering or its causes; its nature is loving-kindness. One of the three wholesome roots.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於苦、苦具，無恚為性；對治瞋恚，作善為業。」《大乘五蘊論》更直接說：「瞋對治，以慈為性。」

**無瞋與不害**：兩者都和慈悲有關。《成唯識論》說不害是「即無瞋」上假立的：「無瞋與樂，不害拔苦」——無瞋是給予快樂的慈，不害是拔除痛苦的悲。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is non-hostility toward suffering and the causes of suffering; it counteracts hatred and produces good." The Pañcaskandhaka says simply: "the antidote to hatred; its nature is loving-kindness."

**Non-hatred and non-harming**: both concern kindness. The Cheng weishi lun treats non-harming as designated on non-hatred: "Non-hatred gives happiness; non-harming removes suffering" — maitrī and karuṇā respectively.

quotes.text: 云何無瞋？於苦、苦具，無恚為性；對治瞋恚，作善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is non-hatred? Its nature is non-hostility toward suffering and its causes; its function is to counteract hatred and produce good.

quotes.text: 云何無瞋？謂瞋對治，以慈為性。
quotes.note_en: What is non-hatred? As the antidote to hatred, its nature is loving-kindness.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ moha「癡」 · a- "not" + moha "delusion"
terms.short_zh: 對事理明白了解；對治愚癡。三善根之一。
terms.short_en: Non-delusion — clear understanding of principles and facts; counteracts delusion. One of the three wholesome roots.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於諸理事，明解為性；對治愚癡，作善為業。」與煩惱「癡」（於諸理事迷闇為性）正好相對。

**無癡與慧**：無癡的體性其實就是善的慧。《成唯識論》討論時指出，無癡以慧為體，但為了顯示善品中對治癡的力量特別殊勝，所以另立為三善根之一。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is clear understanding of principles and facts; it counteracts delusion and produces good" — the exact opposite of the affliction delusion, "darkness about principles and facts".

**Non-delusion and wisdom**: in substance non-delusion is wholesome prajñā. The Cheng weishi lun explains that although it has wisdom as its essence, it is listed separately as a wholesome root to show the special strength of the good in counteracting delusion.

quotes.text: 云何無癡？於諸理事，明解為性；對治愚癡，作善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is non-delusion? Its nature is clear understanding of principles and facts; its function is to counteract delusion and produce good.

quotes.text: 云何無癡？謂癡對治，以其如實正行為性。
quotes.note_en: What is non-delusion? As the antidote to delusion, its nature is correct practice in accordance with reality.

terms.root: pra-√śrambh「放鬆、安息」 · pra-√śrambh "to relax, be calm"
terms.short_zh: 遠離身心的麁重，調暢而堪能；對治惛沈。修定所生的善心所。
terms.short_en: Pliancy — freedom from physical and mental heaviness, so that body and mind are fit for use; counteracts torpor.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「安謂輕安，遠離麁重，調暢身心，堪任為性；對治惛沈，轉依為業。」「麁重」指身心的沉重、不聽使喚；輕安則讓身心輕快、調柔，想修什麼善法都「堪能」去做。

輕安主要在修定時生起，是禪修進步的重要徵兆（七覺支中的「輕安覺支」）。「轉依為業」說明它能轉捨麁重、轉得安適，成為修道轉依的助緣。它直接對治隨煩惱中的「惛沈」。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Pliancy means being far from heaviness, with body and mind fluent and at ease; its nature is fitness for use; it counteracts torpor and brings about transformation of the basis." "Heaviness" is the dull unworkability of body and mind; pliancy makes them light and supple, "fit" for any wholesome task.

It arises chiefly in meditation and is an important sign of progress (the "tranquillity" factor of awakening). Its function of "transforming the basis" means discarding heaviness and gaining ease, supporting the transformation of the path. It directly counteracts the secondary affliction torpor.

quotes.text: 安謂輕安，遠離麁重，調暢身心，堪任為性；對治惛沈，轉依為業。
quotes.note_en: Pliancy means being far from heaviness, with body and mind harmonized and fluent; its nature is fitness for use; its function is to counteract torpor and bring about transformation of the basis.

quotes.text: 云何輕安？謂麁重對治，身心調暢堪能為性。
quotes.note_en: What is pliancy? As the antidote to heaviness, its nature is fluency and fitness of body and mind.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ pramāda「放逸」 · a- "not" + pramāda "heedlessness"
terms.short_zh: 以精進與三善根為體，防惡修善；對治放逸。非別有實體，是假立的善心所。
terms.short_en: Conscientiousness — guarding against evil and cultivating good, based on diligence and the three wholesome roots; counteracts heedlessness. A designated, not separately real, factor.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「不放逸者，精進、三根，於所斷、修，防、修為性；對治放逸，成滿一切世、出世間善事為業。」不放逸不是獨立的心所，而是精進與無貪、無瞋、無癡四法在「防範該斷的惡、修習該修的善」上的作用，**假立**為一個名稱。

佛陀的最後遺言強調的正是不放逸。《長阿含經．遊行經》：「無為放逸，我以不放逸故，自致正覺。」
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots, whose nature is guarding against what is to be abandoned and cultivating what is to be developed; it counteracts heedlessness and fulfils all worldly and transcendent good." It is not a separate entity: the name is **designated** on the working of diligence plus non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion in guarding against evil and cultivating good.

The Buddha's last words stress exactly this. Dīrghāgama, Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra: "Do not be heedless; it was through heedfulness that I attained right awakening."

quotes.text: 不放逸者：精進、三根，於所斷、修，防、修為性；對治放逸，成滿一切世、出世間善事為業。
quotes.note_en: Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots, whose nature is guarding against what is to be abandoned and cultivating what is to be developed; its function is to counteract heedlessness and fulfil all worldly and transcendent good deeds.

quotes.text: 無為放逸，我以不放逸故，自致正覺
quotes.note_en: Do not be heedless. Through heedfulness I myself attained right awakening.

terms.root: upa-√īkṣ「旁觀、不偏」 · upa-√īkṣ "to look on (impartially)"
terms.short_zh: 令心平等、正直、無功用而住；對治掉舉。也是四無量心中的「捨」。
terms.short_en: Equanimity — keeping the mind even, upright and effortlessly settled; counteracts restlessness. Also the fourth immeasurable.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「行捨？精進、三根，令心平等、正直、無功用住為性；對治掉舉，靜住為業。」與不放逸一樣，行捨也是依精進與三善根**假立**的：先離掉舉而「平等」，再離不正而「正直」，最後不必用力而「無功用住」。

**「捨」字要分清**：
- 行捨：屬行蘊的善心所，心的平衡；
- 捨受：受蘊中的「不苦不樂受」，是感受；
- 捨無量：四無量心之一，對一切眾生平等無憎愛的心。
三者梵語都含 upekṣā，但體性與所屬完全不同。

quotes.text: 精進、三根，令心平等、正直、無功用住為性；對治掉舉，靜住為業。
quotes.note_en: Equanimity of formations is diligence and the three roots, whose nature is making the mind even, upright and effortlessly settled; its function is to counteract restlessness and bring about quiet abiding.

quotes.text: 云何為捨？謂即無貪乃至精進。依止此故，獲得所有心平等性，心正直性，心無發悟性。又由此故，於已除遣染污法中，無染安住。
quotes.note_en: What is equanimity? It is non-greed and the rest, up to diligence. Relying on these one attains evenness, uprightness and effortlessness of mind, and, the defiled dharmas having been removed, abides undefiled.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ vihiṃsā「傷害」（《三十頌》作 ahiṃsā） · a- + vihiṃsā "harming" (Triṃśikā: ahiṃsā)
terms.short_zh: 不損惱有情，以無瞋為體、悲愍為用；對治害。
terms.short_en: Non-harming — not injuring beings; its substance is non-hatred and its function compassion. Counteracts harmfulness.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》：「於諸有情，不為損惱，無瞋為性；能對治害，悲愍為業。」不害也是**假立**的：「即無瞋，於有情所不為損惱，假名不害」。

論中對無瞋與不害作了精彩的區分：「無瞋翻對斷物命瞋，不害正違損惱物害。無瞋與樂，不害拔苦。」——無瞋對治的是奪命的瞋恚，給予快樂（慈）；不害對治的是損惱眾生的害心，拔除痛苦（悲）。
terms.detail_en:
Cheng weishi lun: "Its nature is not injuring beings, with non-hatred [as substance]; it counteracts harmfulness and its function is compassion." Non-harming is **designated**: "non-hatred, when it does not injure beings, is provisionally called non-harming."

The treatise draws a fine distinction: "Non-hatred opposes the hatred that takes life; non-harming opposes the harmfulness that torments beings. Non-hatred gives happiness; non-harming removes suffering" — loving-kindness versus compassion.

quotes.text: 云何『不害』？於諸有情，不為損惱，無瞋為性；能對治害，悲愍為業。
quotes.note_en: What is non-harming? Its nature is not injuring beings, being non-hatred; its function is to counteract harmfulness and to be compassionate.

quotes.text: 無瞋，翻對斷物命瞋；不害，正違損惱物害。無瞋與樂；不害拔苦。
quotes.note_en: Non-hatred is the opposite of the hatred that cuts off beings' lives; non-harming directly opposes the harmfulness that torments beings. Non-hatred gives happiness; non-harming removes suffering.

terms.root: 原義「肩、樹幹、大塊、堆聚」 · lit. "shoulder, trunk, mass, heap"
terms.short_zh: 同類法的積聚；佛陀把有情身心分析為色、受、想、行、識五蘊。
terms.short_en: A "heap" of similar dharmas; the Buddha analysed body and mind into five such aggregates.
terms.detail_zh:
梵語 skandha 原義為「肩」「樹幹」「大塊、堆聚」。佛教用來指「同類法的積聚」：凡過去、未來、現在，內、外，粗、細，劣、勝，遠、近的一切色，總為一聚，名為色蘊；受、想、行、識亦然。舊譯作「陰」（五陰、五受陰），玄奘新譯作「蘊」。

五蘊說的主旨在於**無我**：把被執為「我」的身心，分解為五類剎那生滅、依緣而起的法，指出其中找不到常一、主宰的「我」。經中常說「五受陰」（upādāna-skandha，新譯「五取蘊」），強調有漏而被執取的五蘊，正是苦諦的內容。

在百法體系中，五蘊恰好攝盡一切有為法：色蘊攝十一色法；受、想各為一心所；行蘊攝其餘四十九心所與二十四心不相應行；識蘊攝八識。合計 11＋1＋1＋73＋8＝94 法，即百法減去六無為。無為法不在五蘊之內。
terms.detail_en:
Skandha literally means "shoulder", "trunk (of a tree)", or "mass, heap". In Buddhist usage it is a grouping of similar dharmas: all form — past, future or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — is gathered into one heap called the form aggregate, and likewise for feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Older Chinese translations use 陰 (五陰); Xuanzang uses 蘊.

The point of the analysis is **non-self**: what we cling to as "I" is broken down into five kinds of momentary, conditioned phenomena, in none of which a permanent, unitary, controlling self can be found. The sūtras often speak of the "five aggregates of clinging" (upādāna-skandha, 五取蘊): the defiled aggregates, as objects of clinging, are the content of the truth of suffering.

In the Yogācāra hundred-dharma scheme the five aggregates exactly cover all conditioned dharmas: form = 11 material dharmas; feeling and perception = one mental factor each; formations = the remaining 49 mental factors + 24 non-associated formations; consciousness = the 8 consciousnesses. 11 + 1 + 1 + 73 + 8 = 94, i.e. the hundred dharmas minus the six unconditioned ones, which lie outside the aggregates.

quotes.text: 如薄伽梵略說五蘊：一者、色蘊，二者、受蘊，三者、想蘊，四者、行蘊，五者、識蘊。
quotes.note_en: As the Blessed One briefly taught the five aggregates — first, form; second, feeling; third, perception; fourth, formations; fifth, consciousness.

quotes.text: 諸有為法和合聚義是蘊義，如契經言：諸所有色，若過去若未來若現在、若內若外、若麁若細、若劣若勝、若遠若近，如是一切略為一聚，說名色蘊。
quotes.note_en: The meaning of "aggregate" is the gathering-together of conditioned dharmas. As the sūtra says, all form whatsoever — past, future or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all of it taken together as one heap is called the form aggregate.

terms.root: 「形色、形相」 · "form, shape, visible appearance"
terms.short_zh: 物質現象；五蘊之首，即四大種及四大所造色。
terms.short_en: Form/matter — the four great elements and what is derived from them; first of the five aggregates.
terms.detail_zh:
「色」在五蘊中泛指一切物質性的存在，不單指顏色。《雜阿含經》定義為「一切四大及四大造色」：四大種即地、水、火、風，指堅、濕、煖、動四種性質；所造色是依四大而有的物質。《大乘五蘊論》列所造色為五根（眼、耳、鼻、舌、身的淨色根）、五境（色、聲、香、味、所觸一分）與無表色等。

**注意廣狹二義**：作為色蘊，「色」是一切物質；作為十二處、十八界中的「色處／色境」（rūpa-āyatana），則專指眼所見的顏色與形狀（顯色、形色）。

阿毗達磨傳統常以「變礙」解釋色：會變壞，且佔有空間而相互障礙。
terms.detail_en:
In the aggregates, rūpa means all material existence, not just "colour". The Saṃyuktāgama defines it as "the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements": earth, water, fire and wind — the properties of solidity, cohesion, heat and motion — plus secondary matter that depends on them. The Pañcaskandhaka lists derived form as the five sense faculties (the subtle "clear matter" of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body), the five sense objects, and "unmanifest form" (avijñapti).

**Two scopes of one word**: as an aggregate, rūpa is all matter; as one of the twelve sense bases (rūpa-āyatana, 色處), it is only the visible object — colour and shape.

Abhidharma tradition glosses rūpa as that which "changes and obstructs" (變礙): it deteriorates, and it occupies space so as to resist other matter.

quotes.text: 云何色如實知？諸所有色，一切四大及四大造色，是名色。
quotes.note_en: How does one know form as it really is? Whatever form there is — all of it the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements — this is called form.

quotes.text: 云何色蘊？謂四大種及四大種所造諸色。
quotes.note_en: What is the form aggregate? The four great elements and all forms derived from the four great elements.

terms.root: √vid「知、感受」 · √vid "to know, experience"
terms.short_zh: 領納苦、樂、不苦不樂的感受；既是五蘊之一，也是遍行心所之一。
terms.short_en: Feeling — experiencing the pleasant, painful or neutral; both an aggregate and an omnipresent mental factor.
terms.detail_zh:
「受」是與境相遇時產生的苦、樂、不苦不樂（捨）三種感受基調，不是「情緒」的全部。《雜阿含經》說「六受身」：眼觸生受乃至意觸生受——受以觸為緣。

《成唯識論》定義：「領納順、違、俱非境相為性，起愛為業」。受領納可意、不可意、非可意非不可意的境；它的作用是引生愛——對樂受希望不離（合欲），對苦受希望遠離（離欲）。這正是十二因緣「觸緣受、受緣愛」的關鍵一環。

受本來只是一個心所，為什麼在五蘊中單獨立為一蘊？《俱舍論》說受是「諍根」與「生死因」：由貪著受味而貪著諸欲。詳見比較卡「受、想：作為蘊與作為遍行心所」。
terms.detail_en:
Vedanā is the basic hedonic tone — pleasant, painful, or neither — that arises on meeting an object; it is not "emotion" in general. The Saṃyuktāgama speaks of "six classes of feeling": feeling born of eye-contact up to feeling born of mind-contact — feeling is conditioned by contact.

The Cheng weishi lun defines it as "experiencing the agreeable, disagreeable or neutral aspect of an object; its function is to give rise to craving" — the wish not to be parted from pleasure and to be rid of pain. This is the crucial link "contact → feeling → craving" in dependent origination.

Feeling is just one mental factor, so why a separate aggregate? The Abhidharmakośa says feeling is a "root of dispute" and a "cause of saṃsāra": relishing feeling leads to attachment to sense pleasures. See the comparison card on feeling and perception as aggregates vs. omnipresent factors.

schools.name: 南傳阿毗達摩 Theravāda
schools.zh: 受是七個「遍一切心所」之一。
schools.en: One of the seven universal mental factors (sabbacittasādhāraṇa).

quotes.text: 云何受如實知？有六受身——眼觸生受，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸生受，是名受。
quotes.note_en: How does one know feeling as it really is? There are six classes of feeling — feeling born of eye-contact, and of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body- and mind-contact. This is called feeling.

quotes.text: 受謂領納順、違、俱非境相為性，起愛為業，能起合、離、非二欲故。
quotes.note_en: Feeling has as its nature the experiencing of an agreeable, disagreeable or neutral object; its function is to give rise to craving, since it produces the desire for union, for separation, or for neither.

quotes.text: 云何受蘊？謂三領納：一、苦，二、樂，三、不苦不樂。
quotes.note_en: What is the feeling aggregate? The three kinds of experiencing — painful, pleasant, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

terms.root: saṃ-√jñā「合而知、認出」 · saṃ-√jñā "to know together, recognize"
terms.short_zh: 於境取像、辨識特徵並施設名言；五蘊之一，亦為遍行心所。
terms.short_en: Perception/recognition — grasping an object's marks and applying names; an aggregate and an omnipresent factor.
terms.detail_zh:
「想」不是日常中文的「想念、思考」，而是**認取、辨識**：抓取對象的特徵（青黃、長短、男女、怨親等），並與概念連結，因而能「施設種種名言」。《成唯識論》：「想謂於境取像為性，施設種種名言為業」——要先確立對象的界限相狀，才能隨之起種種名稱語言。

**常見誤譯**：把 saṃjñā 譯為 "thought"。佛教心理學中的「思考」更接近「尋、伺」（vitarka, vicāra）；「思」（cetanā）則是意志。想只是「認出這是什麼」。

想與識同根（√jñā）：識是「了別」，總體地覺知對象；想則進一步取其相狀。《俱舍論》說想是「諍根」之一：由顛倒的想而貪著諸見。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃjñā is not "thinking" but **recognition**: seizing an object's distinguishing marks (blue or yellow, long or short, male or female, friend or foe) and linking them with concepts, which makes it possible to "apply all kinds of names and words". The Cheng weishi lun: "its nature is to grasp the image of the object; its function is to set up names and concepts" — one must first fix the boundaries and features of an object before names can follow.

**A common mistranslation** is "thought". Discursive thinking in Buddhist psychology is closer to vitarka/vicāra (尋伺), and cetanā (思) is volition. Saṃjñā simply recognizes "what this is".

Saṃjñā shares its root √jñā with vijñāna: consciousness discerns the object as a whole, perception picks out its features. The Abhidharmakośa calls perception a "root of dispute": distorted perception leads to attachment to views.

schools.name: 俱舍 Sarvāstivāda
schools.zh: 十大地法之一；與受並列為「諍根」，故別立為蘊。
schools.en: One of the ten universal factors; with feeling, a "root of dispute", hence a separate aggregate.

quotes.text: 云何想如實知？謂六想身。云何為六？謂眼觸生想，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸生想，是名想。
quotes.note_en: How does one know perception as it really is? The six classes of perception. Which six? Perception born of eye-contact, and of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body- and mind-contact. This is called perception.

quotes.text: 想謂於境取像為性，施設種種名言為業，謂要安立境分齊相，方能隨起種種名言。
quotes.note_en: Perception has as its nature the grasping of the image of an object, and as its function the setting-up of names and words — only after the defining features of an object are established can names and words arise accordingly.

quotes.text: 想蘊謂能取像為體，即能執取青黃長短、男女怨親、苦樂等相。
quotes.note_en: The perception aggregate is, in essence, the grasping of images — seizing marks such as blue or yellow, long or short, male or female, enemy or friend, pain or pleasure.

terms.root: saṃ-√kṛ「共同 + 作」＝組合、造作 · saṃ-√kṛ "to put together, make"
terms.short_zh: 造作、遷流。行蘊＝受、想以外的一切心所與不相應行（以思為首）；十二因緣之行＝身口意三業；諸行＝一切有為法。
terms.short_en: "Formations". Aggregate — all mental factors other than feeling and perception, plus non-associated formations (led by volition); 12 links — karmic acts of body, speech, mind; "all saṃskāras" — all conditioned things.
terms.detail_zh:
saṃskāra 由 saṃ-（共同）與 √kṛ（作）構成，本義是「把東西組合在一起」。它同時有能動（造作的力量）與所動（被造作者）二面，漢譯為「行」，取造作、遷流之義。這是佛教最多義的術語之一，至少要分清三種用法：

1. **行蘊**：《雜阿含經》以「六思身」定義行蘊（眼觸生思乃至意觸生思）。《俱舍論》解釋：行蘊實際包括色、受、想、識以外的一切有為法；佛只說「思」，是因為「行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝」。《大乘五蘊論》：「除受想，諸餘心法及心不相應行」——在百法中共 49 個心所加 24 個不相應行。
2. **十二因緣第二支「行」**：「緣無明行」。《雜阿含經》：「行有三種——身行、口行、意行」，指由無明推動、能招感後有的業。
3. **諸行（有為法）**：「諸行無常」的「行」是 saṃskāra 的複數，指一切因緣所造作的有為法（saṃskṛta），範圍最廣，包含五蘊全部。

三義互相關連：造作的力量（思、業）產生被造作者（有為法），被造作者又成為再造作的條件——輪迴的動力學就藏在這一個字裡。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃskāra is built from saṃ- ("together") and √kṛ ("make"): "putting together". It has both an active side (the forming force) and a passive side (what is formed). Chinese renders it 行, "activity, flowing on". It is one of the most polysemous Buddhist terms; distinguish at least three uses:

1. **The formations aggregate**: the Saṃyuktāgama defines it as "the six classes of volition" (volition born of eye-contact … mind-contact). The Abhidharmakośa explains that the aggregate actually includes every conditioned dharma other than form, feeling, perception and consciousness; the Buddha names only volition because "saṃskāra means 'forming', and volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — hence foremost". The Pañcaskandhaka: "the remaining mental factors apart from feeling and perception, and the non-associated formations" — 49 mental factors + 24 non-associated formations in the hundred-dharma scheme.
2. **The second of the twelve links**: "ignorance conditions saṃskāra". The Saṃyuktāgama: "saṃskāra is of three kinds — bodily, verbal and mental", i.e. karma driven by ignorance that projects future existence.
3. **All saṃskāras (conditioned things)**: in "all saṃskāras are impermanent", the plural means everything produced by conditions (saṃskṛta) — the widest sense, including all five aggregates.

The three are linked: the forming force (volition, karma) produces what is formed (conditioned dharmas), which in turn become conditions for further forming — the dynamics of saṃsāra in a single word.

schools.name: 南傳阿毗達摩 Theravāda
schools.zh: 行蘊＝五十二心所中除受、想之外的五十個心所。
schools.en: The formations aggregate = 50 of the 52 cetasikas (all except feeling and perception).

schools.name: 俱舍 Sarvāstivāda
schools.zh: 行蘊＝除受、想外的四十四心所＋十四心不相應行。
schools.en: = 44 mental factors (46 minus feeling and perception) + 14 non-associated formations.

schools.name: 唯識 Yogācāra
schools.zh: 行蘊＝四十九心所＋二十四心不相應行，共七十三法。

quotes.text: 云何行如實知？謂六思身——眼觸生思，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸生思，是名為行。
quotes.note_en: How does one know formations as they really are? The six classes of volition — volition born of eye-contact, and of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body- and mind-contact. This is called formations.

quotes.text: 除前及後色、受、想、識，餘一切行名為行蘊。然薄伽梵於契經中說六思身為行蘊者，由最勝故。所以者何？行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝。
quotes.note_en: All saṃskāras other than form, feeling, perception and consciousness are the formations aggregate. The Blessed One described it in the sūtra as the six classes of volition because volition is foremost. Why? Saṃskāra means "forming"; volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — therefore it is foremost.

quotes.text: 云何行蘊？謂除受想，諸餘心法及心不相應行。
quotes.note_en: What is the formations aggregate? The remaining mental factors apart from feeling and perception, and the formations not associated with mind.

quotes.text: 緣無明行者，云何為行？行有三種——身行、口行、意行。
quotes.note_en: "Ignorance conditions formations" — what are formations? Formations are of three kinds: bodily, verbal and mental formations.

terms.mnemonic_zh: 思是將軍，行蘊是軍隊，十二因緣之行是打過的仗，諸行是整個被造作的世界。
terms.mnemonic_en: Volition is the general, the formations aggregate is the army, the 2nd link is the battles already fought, and "all saṃskāras" is the whole world that was built.

terms.root: vi-√jñā「分別 + 知」 · vi-√jñā "to know distinctly, discern"
terms.short_zh: 了別；對境的基本覺知。五蘊之一；唯識學中開為八識。
terms.short_en: Consciousness — the basic discerning awareness of an object; an aggregate, expanded into eight consciousnesses in Yogācāra.
terms.detail_zh:
vi-（分別）＋ √jñā（知），意為「分別地知」。《雜阿含經》以「六識身」定義識：眼識乃至意識，依根與境而生。《大乘五蘊論》：「云何識蘊？謂於所緣境了別為性。」

識與想同根 √jñā：識是「了別」——知道有一個對象並總體地覺知它；想則進一步抓取其相狀。《成唯識論》：「心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相。」

說一切有部認為識即心王，與心、意體一而名異（「集起故名心，思量故名意，了別故名識」）。唯識學另立第七末那識、第八阿賴耶識，合為八識；識蘊即攝百法中的八個心法。在十二因緣中，「識」是第三支（緣行識），《雜阿含經》同樣解作六識身。
terms.detail_en:
vi- ("apart, distinctly") + √jñā ("know"): "knowing distinctly".
