The Saṃyuktāgama defines it as "the six classes of consciousness", eye- through mind-consciousness, arising in dependence on faculty and object. Pañcaskandhaka: "What is the consciousness aggregate? Its nature is to discern its object."

It shares the root √jñā with saṃjñā (perception): consciousness discerns — it knows that there is an object and cognizes it as a whole; perception goes on to grasp its features. The Cheng weishi lun: "mind grasps only the general characteristic of its object; mental factors also grasp particular characteristics."

For the Sarvāstivāda, vijñāna is the "mind-king" (citta), one entity with citta and manas under three names. Yogācāra adds a seventh (manas) and eighth (ālaya-vijñāna) consciousness, and the consciousness aggregate = the eight "mind" dharmas of the hundred. In the twelve links, vijñāna is the third link ("formations condition consciousness"), again glossed as the six classes of consciousness.

quotes.text: 云何識如實知？謂六識身——眼識身，耳、鼻、舌、身、意識身，是名為識身。
quotes.note_en: How does one know consciousness as it really is? The six classes of consciousness — eye-consciousness, and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body- and mind-consciousness. This is called the body of consciousness.

quotes.text: 云何識蘊？謂於所緣境了別為性。
quotes.note_en: What is the consciousness aggregate? Its nature is discerning the object.

terms.root: √cit「覺知」；阿毗達磨另以 √ci「積集」解 · √cit "to perceive"; Abhidharma also glosses from √ci "to accumulate"
terms.short_zh: 心王：了別對境的主體，與心所相對。有部認為心、意、識體一而名異。
terms.short_en: Mind (the "mind-king") — the primary cognizing awareness, contrasted with mental factors; in Abhidharma, citta, manas and vijñāna are one entity with three names.
terms.detail_zh:
字根 √cit（覺知）。阿毗達磨又以 √ci（積集）解釋，所以玄奘譯文說「集起故名心」。《俱舍論》：「集起故名心，思量故名意，了別故名識」——三者體一，只是從不同作用立名。

在心與心所的關係中，心是主（心王），心所是伴。《成唯識論》：心只取對象的「總相」，心所兼取「別相」，如畫師作模、弟子填彩。

**唯識學的分配**：《成唯識論》認為心、意、識三義雖通八識，但「隨勝顯」：第八阿賴耶識集諸法種子、生起諸法，最名為「心」；第七末那識恆審思量、執藏識為我，最名為「意」；前六識於六種境界粗動間斷地了別，最名為「識」。
terms.detail_en:
From √cit ("to perceive"). Abhidharma also explains it from √ci ("to accumulate"), hence Xuanzang's "called citta because it accumulates/gives rise". Abhidharmakośa: "It is called citta because it accumulates, manas because it deliberates, vijñāna because it discerns" — one entity, named by different functions.

Between mind and mental factors, mind is the ruler (心王, "mind-king") and the factors its retinue. Cheng weishi lun: mind grasps only the object's general characteristic; mental factors also grasp particular ones — like a master painter drawing the outline while apprentices fill in colour.

**Yogācāra distribution**: although all three meanings apply to all eight consciousnesses, each name fits one best: the eighth (ālaya) is "citta" because it accumulates the seeds of all dharmas and produces them; the seventh (manas) is "manas" because it constantly and intently deliberates, taking the store-consciousness as a self; the first six are "vijñāna" because they discern their six coarse, intermittent objects.

quotes.text: 集起故名心，思量故名意，了別故名識。
quotes.note_en: It is called citta because it accumulates, manas because it deliberates, vijñāna because it discerns.

quotes.text: 集起名心，思量名意，了別名識，是三別義。如是三義，雖通八識，而隨勝顯。第八名心，集諸法種，起諸法故；第七名意，緣藏識等，恒、審思量，為我等故；餘六名識，於六別境，麁動間斷，了別轉故。
quotes.note_en: Accumulating-and-arising is called citta, deliberating is called manas, discerning is called vijñāna — three distinct meanings. Though all three apply to all eight consciousnesses, each is named by what is most prominent. The eighth is called citta because it accumulates the seeds of all dharmas and gives rise to them; the seventh is called manas because, taking the store-consciousness as its object, it constantly and intently deliberates, [grasping it] as self; the remaining six are called vijñāna because they discern their six separate objects in a coarse, active, intermittent way.

terms.root: cetas「心」→「屬於心的」 · from cetas "mind": "belonging to mind"
terms.short_zh: 「心所有法」：依心而起、與心相應的心理作用，如受、想、思、信、貪等。百法中有五十一種。
terms.short_en: Mental factor — a mental function arising dependent on and associated with mind, e.g. feeling, volition, faith, greed; 51 in Yogācāra.
terms.detail_zh:
caitasika 源自 cetas（心），意為「屬於心的」。玄奘譯為「心所有法」，簡稱「心所」；舊譯「心數」。

《成唯識論》給出三個條件：「恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所」。論中以畫師作比：心如畫師作模，只描出總體輪廓（取總相）；心所如弟子填彩（亦取別相），「助成心事」。

《大乘百法明門論》把五十一心所分為六位：遍行五、別境五、善十一、煩惱六、隨煩惱二十、不定四。《成唯識論》說明其判準：遍行「一切心中定可得」；別境「緣別別境而得生」；善「唯善心中可得生」；煩惱「性是根本煩惱攝」；隨煩惱「唯是煩惱等流性」；不定「於善、染等皆不定」。

**比較**：《俱舍論》立四十六心所（大地法十、大善地法十、大煩惱地法六、大不善地法二、小煩惱地法十、不定法八）；南傳阿毗達摩立五十二心所。
terms.detail_en:
Caitasika derives from cetas ("mind"): "belonging to mind". Xuanzang: 心所有法 "dharmas possessed by mind", short 心所; older translations use 心數.

The Cheng weishi lun gives three conditions: "They always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind, and are bound to mind — hence 'mental factors'." Its simile: mind is like a master painter drawing the outline (grasping the general characteristic); mental factors are like apprentices filling in colour (grasping particular characteristics too), "helping to accomplish the work of mind".

The Hundred Dharmas treatise divides the 51 factors into six categories: 5 omnipresent, 5 object-specific, 11 wholesome, 6 root afflictions, 20 secondary afflictions, 4 indeterminate. The Cheng weishi lun gives the criteria: omnipresent — found in every mind; object-specific — arise only with particular objects; wholesome — arise only in wholesome minds; afflictions — root afflictions by nature; secondary afflictions — outflows of the afflictions; indeterminate — not fixed as wholesome or defiled.

**Comparison**: the Abhidharmakośa has 46 mental factors (10 universal, 10 universal-wholesome, 6 universal-affliction, 2 universal-unwholesome, 10 minor-affliction, 8 indeterminate); Theravāda Abhidhamma has 52.

quotes.text: 恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所，如屬我物，立我所名。心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相，助成心事，得心所名。如畫師、資，作模、填彩。
quotes.note_en: Because they always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind and are bound to mind, they are called mental factors (lit. "what mind possesses"), just as things belonging to me are called "mine". Mind grasps only the general characteristic of its object; mental factors grasp particular characteristics too, helping accomplish the work of mind — hence the name. It is like a master painter and apprentices: one draws the outline, the others fill in the colour.

quotes.text: 第二心所有法，略有五十一種，分為六位：一遍行有五、二別境有五、三善有十一、四煩惱有六、五隨煩惱有二十、六不定有四。
quotes.note_en: Second, the dharmas possessed by mind: briefly 51, in six categories — 5 omnipresent, 5 object-specific, 11 wholesome, 6 afflictions, 20 secondary afflictions, 4 indeterminate.

quotes.text: 如是六位，合五十一。一切心中，定可得故。緣別別境，而得生故。唯善心中，可得生故。性是根本煩惱攝故。唯是煩惱等流性故。於善、染等，皆不定故。
quotes.note_en: These six categories total fifty-one — [respectively] because they are found in every mind; because they arise only with particular objects; because they arise only in wholesome minds; because by nature they are root afflictions; because they are outflows of the afflictions; because they are not fixed as wholesome, defiled, etc.

terms.root: saṃ-√kṛ 的過去分詞「被組合的」 · past participle of saṃ-√kṛ, "put together, made"
terms.short_zh: 由因緣和合而生、有生滅變化的一切法；與無為（asaṃskṛta）相對。
terms.short_en: Conditioned — whatever is produced by causes and conditions and subject to arising and ceasing; opposite of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta).
terms.detail_zh:
saṃskṛta 是 saṃ-√kṛ 的過去分詞，與 saṃskāra（行）同根：saṃskāra 側重「造作」（力量或過程），saṃskṛta 則是「被造作而成的」。（梵語的名稱 Saṃskṛta 也是同一個字，意為「精製的」語言。）

「諸行無常」中的「諸行」（sarve saṃskārāḥ）實際上就是一切有為法。《俱舍論》：「又諸有為法，謂色等五蘊」——五蘊總攝一切有為法，因為它們都是「眾緣聚集共所作」，沒有任何法僅由一緣而生。無為法（如擇滅＝涅槃、虛空）則不在五蘊之內。

**行與法**：三法印「一切行無常，一切法無我，涅槃寂滅」中，「行」只指有為法，「法」則通有為與無為。所以說無常時用「行」，說無我時用「法」——涅槃不是無常，但也不是我。
terms.detail_en:
Saṃskṛta is the past participle of saṃ-√kṛ, sharing its root with saṃskāra (行): saṃskāra stresses the forming (force or process), saṃskṛta is what has been formed. (The name of the Sanskrit language, saṃskṛta, "refined", is the same word.)

The "saṃskāras" of "all saṃskāras are impermanent" are simply all conditioned dharmas. Abhidharmakośa: "The conditioned dharmas are the five aggregates, form and the rest" — the aggregates include every conditioned thing, because all are "made by the coming-together of many conditions"; nothing arises from a single condition. Unconditioned dharmas (such as cessation-through-knowledge, i.e. nirvāṇa, and space) lie outside the aggregates.

**Saṃskāra vs. dharma**: in the three seals "all saṃskāras are impermanent, all dharmas are non-self, nirvāṇa is peace", "saṃskāras" covers only the conditioned, while "dharmas" covers conditioned and unconditioned alike. Impermanence is said of saṃskāras; non-self of all dharmas — nirvāṇa is not impermanent, yet it is not a self either.

quotes.text: 又諸有為法，謂色等五蘊，亦世路言依，有離有事等。論曰：色等五蘊，謂初色蘊乃至識蘊。如是五法具攝有為，眾緣聚集共所作故。無有少法一緣所生。
quotes.note_en: Verse: "The conditioned dharmas are the five aggregates, form and the rest; they are also called paths of time, bases of speech, having an escape, having a cause…" Commentary: the five aggregates, from form to consciousness, include all conditioned dharmas, because they are produced together by the assembly of many conditions; there is no dharma, however small, born from a single condition.

quotes.text: 色無常，受、想、行、識無常，一切行無常，一切法無我，涅槃寂滅。
quotes.note_en: Form is impermanent; feeling, perception, formations and consciousness are impermanent; all saṃskāras are impermanent; all dharmas are non-self; nirvāṇa is peace.

quotes.text: 諸行無常，是生滅法。
quotes.note_en: All saṃskāras are impermanent; they are subject to arising and ceasing.

terms.root: pratītya「依靠之後」（prati-√i）＋ samutpāda「生起」（sam-ut-√pad） · "having depended on" + "arising"
terms.short_zh: 依緣而起：一切現象依條件而生、依條件而滅。「此有故彼有，此起故彼起」。
terms.short_en: Dependent origination — all phenomena arise and cease in dependence on conditions. "When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises."
terms.detail_zh:
pratītya（「依靠之後」，由 prati-√i「走向、依靠」）＋ samutpāda（「生起」）。這是佛陀證悟的核心內容，其通則為「此有故彼有，此起故彼起」；還滅門則是「此無故彼無，此滅故彼滅」。

應用於有情生死，就是**十二因緣**：無明、行、識、名色、六入、觸、受、愛、取、有、生、老死。《雜阿含經》說緣起「若佛出世，若未出世，此法常住，法住法界」——緣起是被發現的法則，不是佛所創造。

**注意區分**「緣起」（pratītyasamutpāda，依緣而起的法則）與「緣生法」（pratītyasamutpanna dharma，依緣而生的現象本身）。《雜阿含經》第296經即分說「因緣法」與「緣生法」。

大乘中觀進一步以緣起說空：凡依緣而起者即無自性。《中論》：「眾因緣生法，我說即是無（空），亦為是假名，亦是中道義。」
terms.detail_en:
pratītya ("having depended on", from prati-√i "go toward, rely on") + samutpāda ("arising"). This is the heart of the Buddha's awakening, stated in general form as "when this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises" — and in reverse, "when this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases".

Applied to the round of birth and death it becomes the **twelve links**: ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, ageing-and-death. The Saṃyuktāgama says dependent origination holds "whether or not a Buddha appears in the world; this Dharma abides constantly" — it is discovered, not invented.

**Distinguish** dependent origination (the principle) from dependently-arisen dharmas (pratītyasamutpanna, the phenomena themselves); Saṃyuktāgama sūtra 296 explicitly separates the two.

Madhyamaka reads dependent origination as emptiness: whatever arises dependently lacks intrinsic nature. Mūlamadhyamakakārikā: "Whatever arises from causes and conditions, I declare to be empty; it is also a dependent designation; this is the middle way."

quotes.text: 云何緣起法法說？謂此有故彼有，此起故彼起，謂緣無明行，乃至純大苦聚集，是名緣起法法說。
quotes.note_en: What is the teaching of dependent origination in brief? When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises — that is, ignorance conditions formations … up to the arising of this whole great mass of suffering.

quotes.text: 云何為因緣法？謂此有故彼有，謂緣無明行，緣行識，乃至如是如是純大苦聚集。云何緣生法？謂無明、行。若佛出世，若未出世，此法常住，法住法界。
quotes.note_en: What is the dharma of causes and conditions? When this exists, that comes to be — ignorance conditions formations, formations condition consciousness … up to the arising of this whole great mass of suffering. What are dependently-arisen dharmas? Ignorance, formations… Whether or not a Buddha appears in the world, this Dharma abides constantly, the stability of Dharma, the realm of Dharma.

quotes.text: 眾因緣生法，我說即是無，亦為是假名，亦是中道義。
quotes.note_en: Dharmas born of causes and conditions — I say they are empty (lit. "non-existent"); this is also a dependent designation; this is also the meaning of the middle way.

terms.root: a-「非」＋ vidyā「明、知」（√vid） · a- "not" + vidyā "knowledge" (√vid)
terms.short_zh: 對真理（四諦、緣起、業果等）的根本迷惑；十二因緣之首，煩惱的根本。
terms.short_en: Ignorance — fundamental delusion about reality (the four truths, dependent origination, karma and result); first of the twelve links, root of the afflictions.
terms.detail_zh:
a-（否定）＋ vidyā（明、知）。無明不是一般的「缺乏知識」，而是對實相的根本迷惑——不只「不知道」，更是「錯知」：把無常執為常、苦執為樂、無我執為我。

《雜阿含經》第298經詳說無明的內容：不知前際、後際，不知業報，不知佛法僧，不知苦集滅道，不知因與因所起法……「於六觸入處，不如實覺知」，總名為「癡闇、無明、大冥」。

在十二因緣中，「緣無明行」——無明推動身、口、意三行（業）。百法中，無明是六根本煩惱之一（《成唯識論》稱為「癡」），與善心所「無癡」相對。唯識學又分與貪等並起的「相應無明」，與獨自生起的「不共無明」。
terms.detail_en:
a- (negation) + vidyā ("knowledge"). Avidyā is not a mere lack of information but a basic misapprehension of reality — not just not-knowing but mis-knowing: taking the impermanent as permanent, suffering as happiness, non-self as self.

Saṃyuktāgama sūtra 298 spells out its content: not knowing the past and future, not knowing karma and its result, not knowing the Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha, not knowing suffering, its origin, cessation and path, not knowing causes and what arises from causes … "not knowing the six bases of contact as they really are" — all this is "delusion, darkness, ignorance, great obscurity".

In the twelve links, "ignorance conditions formations": ignorance drives bodily, verbal and mental karma. In the hundred dharmas, ignorance is one of the six root afflictions (called 癡, moha, in the Cheng weishi lun), opposed to the wholesome factor non-delusion (無癡). Yogācāra distinguishes ignorance "associated" with greed etc. from "independent" ignorance arising on its own.

quotes.text: 彼云何無明？若不知前際、不知後際、不知前後際……不知苦、不知集、不知滅、不知道……於六觸入處，不如實覺知，於彼彼不知、不見、無無間等、癡闇、無明、大冥，是名無明。
quotes.note_en: What is ignorance? Not knowing the past, not knowing the future, not knowing past and future … not knowing suffering, its origin, its cessation, the path … not knowing the six bases of contact as they really are; not knowing, not seeing, not penetrating this and that — delusion, darkness, ignorance, great obscurity: this is called ignorance.

quotes.text: 云何為癡？於諸理、事，迷闇為性；能障無癡，一切雜染所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is delusion? Its nature is darkness about principles and facts; its function is to obstruct non-delusion and to be the basis of all defilement.

quotes.text: 云何無明？謂於業果及諦寶中無智為性。
quotes.note_en: What is ignorance? Its nature is lack of knowledge regarding karma and its results, the truths and the Jewels.

terms.root: √kṛ「作」 · √kṛ "to do, make"
terms.short_zh: 造作、行為；特指由「思」推動、能招感果報的身、語、意行為。
terms.short_en: Action — intentional acts of body, speech and mind, driven by volition, which bring results.
terms.detail_zh:
karman 源自 √kṛ（作），本義「所作、行為」（主格 karma）。佛教把業的本質定在「思」（cetanā）：《俱舍論》：「世別由業生，思及思所作，思即是意業，所作謂身語。」世界的種種差別，都由有情的業而生，而非由一主宰者創造。

業分身、語、意三業；契經又說「思業」（意中的思惟決意）與「思已業」（決意之後發動身語的行為）。

**業與行**：十二因緣中的「行」（身行、口行、意行）就是由無明推動所造的業；業的餘勢將招感未來的識、名色等果。唯識學認為業力以「種子」形式熏習於阿賴耶識，待緣成熟而感果。
terms.detail_en:
Karman comes from √kṛ ("to do"): "what is done, action" (nominative karma). Buddhism locates the essence of karma in volition: Abhidharmakośa, "The variety of the world is born of karma — volition and what volition produces. Volition is mental karma; what it produces is bodily and verbal karma." The world's variety comes from beings' actions, not from a single creator.

Karma is bodily, verbal or mental; the sūtra also distinguishes "volition-karma" (the deciding in mind) from "karma after having willed" (the bodily and verbal acts that follow the decision).

**Karma and saṃskāra**: the "formations" of the twelve links (bodily, verbal, mental) are precisely karma driven by ignorance; its residual force projects future consciousness, name-and-form and so on. Yogācāra holds that karma is stored as "seeds" imprinted in the ālaya-vijñāna, ripening when conditions come together.

quotes.text: 此所由業其體是何？謂心所思及思所作。故契經說：有二種業，一者思業、二思已業，思已業者謂思所作。如是二業分別為三，謂即有情身、語、意業。
quotes.note_en: What is the essence of the karma from which these arise? The mental factor volition and what volition produces. Hence the sūtra says there are two kinds of karma — volition, and karma after having willed, which is what volition produces. These two are divided into three: the bodily, verbal and mental karma of beings.

terms.root: sarva「一切」＋ traga「行往」 · sarva "all" + traga "going" = "going everywhere"
terms.short_zh: 遍一切心的五個心所：作意、觸、受、想、思——任何一念心生起時必定同時具有。
terms.short_en: The five mental factors present in every moment of mind — attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition.
terms.detail_zh:
《成唯識論》以「一切心中，定可得故」為遍行的判準：無論善、惡、無記，無論八識中哪一識，只要心生起，這五個心所必然同時生起。唯識注疏更以「四一切」說明：遍一切性、一切地、一切時、一切俱。

五者構成認知最基本的流程：**作意**警覺心、令其趣向對象 → 根、境、識三者和合而有**觸** → **受**領納苦樂 → **想**取相、安立名言 → **思**驅役心去造作。

次序：《大乘百法明門論》作「作意、觸、受、想、思」；《成唯識論》作「觸、作意、受、想、思」。

**比較**：《俱舍論》的「大地法」有十個（受、想、思、觸、欲、慧、念、作意、勝解、三摩地）。唯識學把其中欲、勝解、念、定、慧五者移為「別境」，理由是它們只在緣特定境時生起，並非每一念心都有。南傳阿毗達摩則立七個遍一切心所：觸、受、想、思、一境性、命根、作意。
terms.detail_en:
The Cheng weishi lun's criterion for the omnipresent factors is that they "are found in every mind without fail": whether the mind is wholesome, unwholesome or neutral, and whichever of the eight consciousnesses it is, these five arise with it. Later commentaries explain this with the "four alls": present in every moral quality, every realm, every time, and all together.

Together they form the most basic cognitive sequence: **attention** alerts the mind and turns it toward the object → faculty, object and consciousness meet as **contact** → **feeling** registers pleasant/painful/neutral → **perception** grasps features and names → **volition** drives the mind to act.

Order: the Hundred Dharmas treatise lists attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition; the Cheng weishi lun lists contact first.

**Comparison**: the Abhidharmakośa has ten "universal" factors (mahābhūmika): feeling, perception, volition, contact, desire-to-act, wisdom, mindfulness, attention, resolve, concentration. Yogācāra moves five of them — desire-to-act, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom — to the "object-specific" category, because they arise only with particular objects, not in every mind. Theravāda Abhidhamma has seven universals: contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, life-faculty, attention.

quotes.text: 此識與幾心所相應？常與觸、作意、受、想、思相應。阿賴耶識無始時來乃至未轉，於一切位恒與此五心所相應，以是遍行心所攝故。
quotes.note_en: With how many mental factors is this (store) consciousness associated? Always with contact, attention, feeling, perception and volition. From beginningless time until it is transformed, the ālaya-vijñāna is in every state associated with these five, because they belong to the omnipresent mental factors.

quotes.text: 一遍行五者，一作意、二觸、三受、四想、五思。
quotes.source_en: Mahāyāna Hundred Dharmas Treatise (Vasubandhu), tr. Xuanzang
quotes.note_en: First, the five omnipresent: 1 attention, 2 contact, 3 feeling, 4 perception, 5 volition.

quotes.text: 如是緣眼、色，生眼識，三事和合觸，觸俱生受、想、思。
quotes.note_en: Thus, conditioned by eye and form, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; together with contact arise feeling, perception and volition.

terms.root: √spṛś「觸」 · √spṛś "to touch"
terms.short_zh: 根、境、識三和合時令心、心所觸對境界的心所；受、想、思的所依。
terms.short_en: Contact — the meeting of faculty, object and consciousness that brings mind into touch with its object; the basis of feeling, perception and volition.
terms.detail_zh:
觸不是物理上的碰觸，而是一個心所：當根（如眼根）、境（色）、識（眼識）三者相應時，觸使心與心所接觸對象。《雜阿含經》以兩手相擊出聲為喻：「譬如兩手和合相對作聲。如是緣眼、色，生眼識，三事和合觸，觸俱生受、想、思。」

《成唯識論》：「觸謂三和分別變異，令心、心所觸境為性，受、想、思等所依為業。」「所依為業」說明觸是受、想、思生起的依據——這也是十二因緣「六入緣觸、觸緣受」的心理學基礎。

**學派差異**：經部認為觸只是三事和合本身，不另有實體；說一切有部與唯識則認為觸是別立的實有心所。
terms.detail_en:
Contact is not physical touching but a mental factor: when faculty (e.g. the eye), object (visible form) and consciousness (eye-consciousness) come together, contact brings mind and mental factors into touch with the object. The Saṃyuktāgama compares it to two hands clapping to make a sound: "conditioned by eye and form, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; together with contact arise feeling, perception and volition."

Cheng weishi lun: "Contact is the concurrence of the three, [with their] correspondence and modification; its nature is to bring mind and mental factors into contact with the object; its function is to be the support of feeling, perception, volition and so on." Being their "support" is the psychological basis of the links "six sense bases → contact → feeling".

**School difference**: the Sautrāntikas held that contact is nothing but the concurrence of the three; the Sarvāstivāda and Yogācāra treat it as a distinct, real mental factor.

quotes.text: 譬如兩手和合相對作聲。如是緣眼、色，生眼識，三事和合觸，觸俱生受、想、思。
quotes.note_en: Just as two hands clapping together make a sound, so, conditioned by eye and form, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; together with contact arise feeling, perception and volition.

quotes.text: 觸謂三和分別變異，令心、心所觸境為性，受、想、思等所依為業。謂根、境、識更相隨順，故名三和。
quotes.note_en: Contact is the concurrence of the three with its modification; its nature is to bring mind and mental factors into contact with the object, and its function is to serve as the support of feeling, perception, volition, etc. Faculty, object and consciousness conform to one another — hence "concurrence of the three".

quotes.text: 云何為觸？謂三和合分別為性。
quotes.note_en: What is contact? Its nature is the discerning that comes from the concurrence of the three.

terms.root: manas「意」＋ kāra「作」 · manas "mind" + kāra "making" — "making in mind"
terms.short_zh: 警覺心、引心趣向所緣境的注意作用。
terms.short_en: Attention — alerting the mind and turning it toward its object.
terms.detail_zh:
manas（意）＋ kāra（作），字面是「作於意中」。《成唯識論》：「作意謂能警心為性，於所緣境，引心為業」，並解釋：「謂此警覺，應起心種，引令趣境，故名作意」——在種子說裡，作意喚醒應當生起的心之種子，引導它朝向對象。

論中破斥兩種異說：有人說作意是「令心迴趣異境」，或「於一境持心令住」。論主指出，這樣就與「定」無別，便不能是遍行。可見作意只是最初的**轉向**；持續專注屬於別境中的「定」（samādhi）。

修行語境中常說「如理作意」（yoniśo manaskāra）與「非理作意」：以正確或錯誤的方式注意對象，決定了煩惱是生起還是止息。
terms.detail_en:
manas ("mind") + kāra ("making"): literally "making [something] in the mind". Cheng weishi lun: "Attention has as its nature the alerting of mind, and as its function the leading of mind toward its object", explaining that it "alerts the seeds of mind that are due to arise and leads them toward the object" — in seed theory, attention awakens the mental seeds and directs them.

The treatise rejects two alternative views — that attention "turns the mind to a different object" or "holds the mind on one object". If so, it would be no different from concentration and could not be omnipresent. So attention is only the initial **turning toward**; sustained focus belongs to concentration (samādhi), an object-specific factor.

In practice contexts one hears of "appropriate attention" (yoniśo manaskāra, 如理作意) and inappropriate attention: how one attends to an object decides whether afflictions arise or cease.

quotes.text: 作意謂能警心為性，於所緣境，引心為業；謂此警覺，應起心種，引令趣境，故名作意。
quotes.note_en: Attention has as its nature the alerting of mind, and as its function the leading of mind toward its object: it alerts the seeds of mind that are due to arise and leads them toward the object — hence it is called attention.

quotes.text: 有說：令心迴趣異境，或於一境，持心令住，故名作意。彼俱非理，應非遍行，不異定故。
quotes.note_en: Some say it is called attention because it turns the mind to a different object, or holds the mind fixed on one object. Both views are wrong: then it would not be omnipresent, since it would not differ from concentration.

quotes.text: 云何作意？謂能令心發悟為性。
quotes.note_en: What is attention? Its nature is to make the mind awaken [to its object].

terms.root: √cit「思、覺察」 · √cit "to perceive, intend"
terms.short_zh: 令心造作的意志作用；遍行心所之一，行蘊的核心，也是「業」的本體。
terms.short_en: Volition — the factor that makes mind act; omnipresent, the core of the formations aggregate, and the essence of karma.
terms.detail_zh:
源自 √cit（思、覺察）。《成唯識論》：「思謂令心造作為性，於善品等役心為業，謂能取境正因等相，驅役自心令造善等。」如將軍驅使士兵，思驅使心與其他心所趨向善、惡等行為。

思有兩個關鍵角色：

1. **遍行**：每一念心都有思——即使最微弱的心念，也帶有某種趨向。所以思不只是有意識的「決定」。
2. **業的本體**：《俱舍論》頌：「世別由業生，思及思所作，思即是意業，所作謂身語。」契經說二業：「思業」與「思已業」。意業就是思本身；身、語業是思所發動的「思所作」。所以佛法論業，重在動機。

**思與行蘊**：經典以「六思身」定義行蘊，因為在行蘊諸法中思「造作義強，故為最勝」。但行蘊並不等於思——詳見比較卡「行與思」。
terms.detail_en:
From √cit ("to perceive, think"). Cheng weishi lun: "Volition has as its nature making the mind act, and as its function directing the mind toward the wholesome, etc.: it grasps the features of the object, such as whether it is a right cause, and drives one's own mind to do good and so on." Like a general commanding troops, volition drives mind and the other factors toward wholesome or unwholesome action.

Volition has two key roles:

1. **Omnipresent**: every moment of mind contains volition — even the faintest thought has some directedness. So cetanā is not just conscious "deciding".
2. **The essence of karma**: Abhidharmakośa verse: "The variety of the world arises from karma — volition and what is done by volition. Volition is mental karma; what it produces is bodily and verbal karma." The sūtra speaks of two karmas: "volition" and "the karma after having willed". Mental karma is volition itself; bodily and verbal karma are what volition sets in motion. This is why Buddhist ethics centres on intention.

**Volition and the formations aggregate**: the sūtras define the aggregate as "six classes of volition" because volition is "strongest in forming, hence foremost" — but the aggregate is not the same as volition. See the comparison card "saṃskāra vs. cetanā".

schools.name: 南傳 Theravāda
schools.zh: 《增支部》著名經句：「諸比丘！我說思即是業」（cetanāhaṃ bhikkhave kammaṃ vadāmi）。
schools.en: The famous Aṅguttara line: "Monks, it is volition that I call karma" (cetanāhaṃ bhikkhave kammaṃ vadāmi).

quotes.text: 思謂令心造作為性，於善品等役心為業，謂能取境正因等相，驅役自心令造善等。
quotes.note_en: Volition has as its nature making the mind act, and as its function directing the mind in wholesome matters and so on; it grasps the features of the object such as right causes, and drives one's own mind to do good, etc.

quotes.text: 世別由業生，思及思所作，思即是意業，所作謂身語。
quotes.note_en: The variety of the world is born of karma — volition and what volition produces. Volition is mental karma; what it produces is bodily and verbal karma.

quotes.text: 云何為思？謂於功德過失及俱相違，令心造作，意業為性。
quotes.note_en: What is volition? With regard to merits, faults and what is neither, it makes the mind act; its nature is mental karma.

comparisons.summary_zh: 勝解是認知上的「印持確定」，可正可邪；信是以「心淨」為性的善心所，對實、德、能深忍樂欲。英譯都可能作 conviction，但體性完全不同。
comparisons.summary_en: Resolve is cognitive "sealing" certainty, which may be right or wrong; faith is a wholesome factor whose nature is clarity of mind, accepting and delighting in the real, virtuous and capable. Both get translated "conviction", yet they differ entirely.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**認知 vs 情意**：勝解是「我確定了」——對已判定的事蓋章認可，他人說不動。它像法官宣判，本身不問對錯：堅信錯誤理論的人也有強烈的勝解。信則以「心淨」為性，含有信忍（接受）、信樂（歡喜）、信欲（嚮往）三面，必定是善的。

**互相配合**：修行中兩者常同時出現——經由聞思而對正法確定（勝解），同時心生澄淨歡喜（信）。但只有勝解而無信，可能流於冷硬的自以為是；只有信而無勝解，則易被動搖。

**相反**：勝解的反面是疑（猶豫不決）；信的反面是不信（心穢、懶惰之依）。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Cognitive vs affective**: resolve is "I am certain" — sealing what has been decided so no one can talk one out of it. Like a judge's verdict, it is not in itself right or wrong: a believer in a false theory can have strong resolve. Faith has clarity of mind as its nature, with acceptance, delight and aspiration, and is always wholesome.

**Working together**: in practice they often arise together — through study and reflection one becomes certain of the Dharma (resolve) while the mind grows clear and glad (faith). Resolve without faith can harden into cold self-righteousness; faith without resolve is easily shaken.

**Opposites**: resolve is opposed by hesitation (doubt); faith by faithlessness (turbidity, the basis of laziness).

quotes.text: 云何勝解？於決定境，印持為性，不可引轉為業。
quotes.note_en: What is resolve? Its nature is confirming and holding to an ascertained object; its function is that it cannot be drawn away.

quotes.text: 云何為信？於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲，心淨為性；對治不信，樂善為業。
quotes.note_en: What is faith? Its nature is deep acceptance, delight and aspiration toward the real, the virtuous and the capable, with clarity of mind; its function is to counteract faithlessness and delight in the good.

questions.q_zh: 勝解可以是錯誤的（邪勝解）。
questions.q_en: Resolve can be mistaken (wrong resolve).
questions.explain_zh: 勝解只是印持決定境，所印持的可能是邪說。
questions.explain_en: Resolve merely seals what is ascertained, which may be a wrong teaching.

questions.q_zh: 信的體性是？
questions.q_en: What is the nature of faith?
questions.explain_zh: 信「心淨為性」。
questions.explain_en: Faith has "clarity of mind" as its nature.

questions.q_zh: 《成唯識論》所說信的三種對象是？
questions.q_en: What are the three objects of faith in the Cheng weishi lun?

options.en: the real, the virtuous, the capable

questions.explain_zh: 「於實、德、能，深忍、樂、欲。」三寶屬於「德」。
questions.explain_en: "Toward the real, the virtuous and the capable"; the Three Jewels fall under "the virtuous".

questions.q_zh: 勝解的反面主要是？
questions.q_en: Resolve is chiefly opposed by…
questions.explain_zh: 勝解於決定境印持；疑則猶豫不能決定。
questions.explain_en: Resolve seals what is decided; doubt cannot decide.

comparisons.title_en: The four indeterminate factors — regret, sleep, inquiry, investigation
comparisons.summary_zh: 這四者不像遍行那樣遍一切心，不像別境那樣定遍一切地，也不固定為善或染，故名「不定」。其善惡由所伴隨的心決定。
comparisons.summary_en: These four are not in every mind like the omnipresent, not in every realm like the object-specific, and not fixed as wholesome or defiled — hence "indeterminate". Their quality depends on the mind they accompany.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**為何叫「不定」**：《成唯識論》：「悔、眠、尋、伺於善、染等皆不定故，非如觸等定遍心故，非如欲等定遍地故，立不定名。」三個「不」：不像遍行遍一切心，不像別境遍一切地（界地），善惡也不固定。

**二各二**：《唯識三十頌》說「不定謂悔、眠，尋、伺二各二」。論師對「二各二」有不同解釋，一說悔眠為一組、尋伺為一組，每組又各分染淨二類。

**修行關聯**：悔與掉舉合為「掉悔蓋」，眠與惛沈合為「惛眠蓋」；尋伺的止息則標誌從初禪進入二禪。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Why "indeterminate"**: Cheng weishi lun: "Regret, sleep, inquiry and investigation are not fixed as wholesome, defiled, etc.; unlike contact and the rest they are not in every mind; unlike aspiration and the rest they are not in every realm — hence indeterminate." Three "nots": not universal like the omnipresent, not in all realms like the object-specific, not fixed in moral quality.

**"Two, each two"**: the Thirty Verses say "the indeterminate are regret and sleep, inquiry and investigation — two, each two". Commentators differ; one reading: regret-sleep and inquiry-investigation form two pairs, each further divided into defiled and pure.

**In practice**: regret joins restlessness in the hindrance "restlessness and remorse"; sleep joins torpor in "torpor and sleep"; the stilling of inquiry and investigation marks the passage from the first to the second dhyāna.

quotes.text: 悔、眠、尋、伺於善、染等皆不定故，非如觸等定遍心故，非如欲等定遍地故，立不定名。
quotes.note_en: Regret, sleep, inquiry and investigation are not fixed as wholesome, defiled, etc.; unlike contact and the rest they are not certainly in every mind, and unlike aspiration and the rest they are not certainly in every realm — hence they are called indeterminate.

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一個不是不定心所？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT an indeterminate factor?
questions.explain_zh: 惛沈是大隨煩惱。四不定：悔、眠、尋、伺。
questions.explain_en: Torpor is a major secondary affliction. The four indeterminate are regret, sleep, inquiry, investigation.

questions.q_zh: 後悔自己做了壞事，這種「悔」是善的。
questions.q_en: Regretting a wrong one has done is wholesome regret.
questions.explain_zh: 悔的善惡由所悔之事決定；悔惡是善。
questions.explain_en: Regret takes its quality from what is regretted; regretting evil is wholesome.

questions.q_zh: 惡作（悔）的「業」是？
questions.q_en: What is the function of regret?
questions.explain_zh: 「悔謂惡作……追悔為性，障止為業。」眠則「障觀為業」。
questions.explain_en: Regret "obstructs calm"; sleep "obstructs insight".

questions.q_zh: 「不定」的理由不包括下列哪一項？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT a reason these factors are called indeterminate?

options.en: not fixed as wholesome or defiled

questions.explain_zh: 論中列出的是前三點。
questions.explain_en: The treatise gives the first three reasons.

comparisons.title_zh: 不放逸與精進；放逸與懈怠
comparisons.title_en: Conscientiousness vs. diligence; heedlessness vs. laziness
comparisons.summary_zh: 精進與懈怠是實有的心所；不放逸與放逸則是「組合」出來的：不放逸＝精進＋三善根（防惡修善），放逸＝懈怠＋貪瞋癡（不防不修）。
comparisons.summary_en: Diligence and laziness are real factors; conscientiousness and heedlessness are "composites" — conscientiousness = diligence + the three wholesome roots (guarding and cultivating), heedlessness = laziness + greed, hatred, delusion (neither guarding nor cultivating).

cells.en: Letting go — no guarding or cultivating

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**精進是油門，不放逸是方向盤加煞車**。精進讓人在善法上勇猛向前；但光有衝勁還不夠，還需要「防」（守住不讓惡生起）與「修」（培養善法），而這需要無貪、無瞋、無癡的配合。精進加上三善根共同發揮「防惡修善」的作用，就叫不放逸。

**反面也對稱**：懈怠是實有的懶惰；放逸則是懈怠加上貪瞋癡，使人既不防惡、也不修善，「縱蕩為性」。

**佛陀的遺言**：臨入滅前，佛陀說「無為放逸，我以不放逸故，自致正覺」。不放逸被視為一切善法的總持。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Diligence is the accelerator; conscientiousness is steering plus brakes.** Diligence drives one forward in the good; but drive alone is not enough — one also needs to "guard" (keep evil from arising) and "cultivate" (develop the good), which requires non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion. Diligence working with the three roots to guard and cultivate is called conscientiousness.

**The opposites mirror this**: laziness is real sluggishness; heedlessness is laziness plus greed, hatred and delusion, so that one neither guards against evil nor cultivates good — "letting go".

**The Buddha's last words**: "Do not be heedless; through heedfulness I attained right awakening." Conscientiousness is regarded as the sum of all good dharmas.

quotes.text: 不放逸者：精進、三根，於所斷、修，防、修為性；對治放逸，成滿一切世、出世間善事為業。
quotes.note_en: Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots, whose nature is guarding against what is to be abandoned and cultivating what is to be developed; its function is to counteract heedlessness and fulfil all worldly and transcendent good deeds.

quotes.text: 謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡，不能防修染淨品法，總名放逸，非別有體。
quotes.note_en: That is, laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion, being unable to guard against and cultivate defiled and pure dharmas, is collectively called heedlessness; it has no separate substance.

questions.q_zh: 不放逸是依哪些法假立的？
questions.q_en: On which dharmas is conscientiousness designated?

options.en: diligence and the three wholesome roots

questions.explain_zh: 「不放逸者：精進、三根……」
questions.explain_en: "Conscientiousness is diligence and the three roots…"

questions.q_zh: 放逸是依哪些法假立的？
questions.q_en: On which dharmas is heedlessness designated?

options.en: it is a separate real factor

questions.explain_zh: 「謂由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡……總名放逸，非別有體。」
questions.explain_en: "Laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion … collectively called heedlessness."

questions.q_zh: 懈怠與精進都是實有的心所。
questions.q_en: Laziness and diligence are both real factors.
questions.explain_zh: 論中判懈怠「定是實有」；精進亦實。
questions.explain_en: The treatise rules laziness definitely real; diligence is real too.

questions.q_zh: 熱衷於做壞事，是否屬於「精進」？
questions.q_en: Is zealous engagement in harmful acts a form of diligence?

options.en: yes, because it is hard work
no — the treatise calls this "also laziness"

questions.explain_zh: 「於諸染事而策勤者，亦名懈怠，退善法故。」
questions.explain_en: "Exerting oneself in defiled affairs is also called laziness, because the good declines."

comparisons.title_zh: 迷與錯：無明（癡）、惡見、疑、不正知與慧
comparisons.title_en: Not knowing and knowing wrongly — ignorance, wrong view, doubt, non-alertness and wisdom
comparisons.summary_zh: 無明是「迷闇」（不明）；惡見是「染慧」（錯誤推度）；疑是「猶豫」（不能決定）；不正知是對當下行為的「謬解」。它們都與「知」有關，但病根不同；慧本身則通善惡。
comparisons.summary_en: Ignorance is darkness (not seeing); wrong view is defiled discernment (reasoning wrongly); doubt is vacillation (not deciding); non-alertness is misreading present conduct. All concern knowing, with different pathologies; prajñā itself can go either way.

cells.zh: 與慧相反；善的對治是無癡

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**四種「不知」的差別**：
- **無明**是根本的「暗」——對事理根本不明白。它是「一切雜染所依」，其他煩惱都在它的基礎上生起。
- **惡見**不是不想，而是想錯了：「顛倒推度，染慧為性」。有身見的人對「我」有一套清楚的推理，只是推錯了。
- **疑**是在真理面前猶豫不決，不肯下判斷。
- **不正知**是在身、語、意的當下行為中覺察錯誤，因而違犯。

**慧的兩面**：慧是別境心所，「簡擇為性，斷疑為業」。如理的慧能斷疑、破無明；而惡見恰恰就是染污的慧。所以佛法說的不是「多思考」就好，而是要「如理」思考。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Four kinds of "not knowing"**:
- **Ignorance** is basic darkness — not understanding at all. It is "the basis of all defilement"; the other afflictions arise on it.
- **Wrong view** is not failing to think but thinking wrongly: "perverse reasoning, defiled discernment". Someone holding self-view has a clear argument for a self — just a wrong one.
- **Doubt** is hesitating before the truth, refusing to judge.
- **Non-alertness** misreads one's present bodily, verbal and mental conduct, and so one transgresses.

**Two faces of prajñā**: prajñā is an object-specific factor, "discrimination by nature, cutting off doubt by function". Sound discernment cuts off doubt and dispels ignorance, yet wrong view is exactly defiled discernment. So the point is not "think more" but "think in accord with reality".

quotes.text: 云何為癡？於諸理、事，迷闇為性；能障無癡，一切雜染所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is delusion? Its nature is darkness about principles and facts; its function is to obstruct non-delusion and to be the basis of all defilement.

quotes.text: 云何惡見？於諸諦理，顛倒推度，染慧為性；能障善見，招苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is wrong view? Its nature is defiled discernment that reasons perversely about the truths; its function is to obstruct good view and bring suffering.

questions.q_zh: 哪一個煩惱的體性本身就是「慧」（染慧）？
questions.q_en: Which affliction has (defiled) prajñā as its very nature?
questions.explain_zh: 惡見「顛倒推度，染慧為性」。
questions.explain_en: Wrong view is "perverse reasoning, with defiled discernment as nature".

questions.q_zh: 被稱為「一切雜染所依」的是？
questions.q_en: Which is called "the basis of all defilement"?
questions.explain_zh: 癡「能障無癡，一切雜染所依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Delusion "obstructs non-delusion and is the basis of all defilement".

questions.q_zh: 對四諦猶豫不決，不知是否該相信——這是？
questions.q_en: Wavering about the four truths, not knowing whether to accept them — this is…
questions.explain_zh: 疑「於諸諦理，猶豫為性」。
questions.explain_en: Doubt is "vacillation about the truths".

questions.q_zh: 慧作為心所，必定是善的。
questions.q_en: As a mental factor, prajñā is always wholesome.
questions.explain_zh: 慧屬別境，通善惡；惡見即是染慧。
questions.explain_en: Prajñā is object-specific and variable; wrong view is defiled prajñā.

questions.q_zh: 說話時沒有覺察自己正在口出惡言，事後才發現——這主要是？
questions.q_en: One does not notice while speaking that one's words are harsh, realizing only afterwards. Chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 不正知「於身語意現前行中不正依住」，導致毀犯。
questions.explain_en: Non-alertness is "not abiding correctly in present conduct of body, speech and mind", leading to transgression.

comparisons.summary_zh: 欲是中性的「希望」，可以希求善法（善法欲）；貪是染污的「染著」，是根本煩惱。不可把佛法說的「斷貪」誤解為「斷一切欲」。
comparisons.summary_en: Chanda is neutral wishing and can aim at the good (wholesome aspiration); rāga is defiled attachment, a root affliction. "Abandon greed" does not mean "abandon every wish".

cells.en: Attachment to existence and its means
Can be wholesome, unwholesome or neutral

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**同樣是「想要」，性質不同**。欲只是希望、意向，本身無善惡：想證悟、想幫助眾生是善法欲；想吃午飯是無記的欲；對五欲境的貪求則與貪相應。貪則不同，它的本質是「染著」——黏住不放，必然帶來苦。

**修行不是消滅動力**。《成唯識論》說欲是「勤依」：沒有想要成就的意欲，就不會精進。所以佛法要斷的是貪，而要培養的是對善法的欲。

**中文陷阱**：漢譯「欲」字常兼指兩者（如「欲界」「五欲」「貪欲」）。讀經時要看上下文：作為別境心所的「欲」（chanda）是中性的；「貪欲」（kāma-rāga）則是煩惱。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Both are "wanting", with different natures.** Chanda is just wishing or intending, morally neutral in itself: wishing for awakening or to help beings is wholesome aspiration; wanting lunch is neutral; craving sense objects goes together with greed. Rāga is different: its essence is attachment — sticking fast — which inevitably brings suffering.

**Practice does not kill motivation.** The Cheng weishi lun calls chanda "the support of effort": without aspiration there is no diligence. So Buddhism abandons greed but cultivates aspiration toward the good.

**A Chinese trap**: 欲 is used for both (欲界 "desire realm", 五欲 "five sense pleasures", 貪欲 "sensual greed"). Read the context: the object-specific factor 欲 (chanda) is neutral; 貪欲 (kāma-rāga) is an affliction.

quotes.text: 云何為欲？於所樂境，希望為性，勤依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is aspiration? Its nature is wishing for a desired object; its function is to serve as the support of effort.

quotes.text: 云何為貪？於有、有具，染著為性；能障無貪，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is greed? Its nature is attachment to existence and the means of existence; its function is to obstruct non-greed and produce suffering.

questions.q_zh: 別境心所「欲」本身必定是不善的。
questions.q_en: The object-specific factor chanda is necessarily unwholesome.
questions.explain_zh: 欲通善、惡、無記；希求善法的是善法欲。
questions.explain_en: Chanda may be wholesome, unwholesome or neutral.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，欲的「業」（作用）是？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what is the function of chanda?
questions.explain_zh: 「希望為性，勤依為業。」
questions.explain_en: "Its nature is wishing; its function is supporting effort."

questions.q_zh: 「想要證悟」屬於？
questions.q_en: "Wishing to attain awakening" is…
questions.explain_zh: 對善法的希求是善法欲，是精進的所依。
questions.explain_en: Wishing for the good is wholesome aspiration, the support of diligence.

questions.q_zh: 在說一切有部，「欲」屬於哪一類？
questions.q_en: In the Sarvāstivāda, chanda belongs to…
questions.explain_zh: 有部列欲為十大地法之一；唯識移入別境。
questions.explain_en: The Sarvāstivāda lists it among the ten universals; Yogācāra moves it to object-specific.

comparisons.summary_zh: 心是主，取總相；心所是伴，兼取別相——如畫師作模、弟子填彩。心所恒依心起、與心相應、繫屬於心。
comparisons.summary_en: Mind is the ruler and grasps the general characteristic; mental factors are its retinue and also grasp particulars — like a master painter outlining and apprentices colouring. Factors always arise dependent on, associated with, and bound to mind.

cells.zh: 受蘊、想蘊，其餘 49 個歸行蘊
cells.en: Feeling, perception; the other 49 in formations

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**心所的三個條件。** 《成唯識論》：「恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所。」心所不能離心單獨生起；它與心同時、同緣、相應而起；它屬於心，就像「屬我之物」叫做「我所」。

**總相與別相。** 心只把握對象的整體（總相）；心所除了總體之外，還把握種種特殊面向（別相）——受把握其可意與否，想把握其相狀，思把握其正因與否。所以說心所「助成心事」。

**相應的五義。** 《俱舍論》頌說心與心所「相應義有五」：所依、所緣、行相、時、事五者平等——同依一根、同緣一境、行相相似、同時生起、各一體而相伴。

**心、意、識。** 在說一切有部，心、意、識是同一體的三個名稱；在唯識，三名雖通八識，但第八名心、第七名意、前六名識。無論哪一說，它們都屬「心」一邊，而不是心所。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Three conditions for a mental factor.** Cheng weishi lun: "They always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind, and are bound to mind — hence 'what mind possesses'." A factor cannot arise apart from mind; it arises simultaneously, with the same object, in association with it; and it belongs to mind as "mine" belongs to "me".

**General vs. particular characteristics.** Mind grasps the object as a whole; mental factors grasp particular aspects as well — feeling its agreeableness, perception its features, volition whether it is a right cause — so they "help accomplish the work of mind".

**Five senses of "association".** The Abhidharmakośa verse says mind and factors are "associated in five respects": same basis (faculty), same object, similar mode of apprehension, same time, and each one a single entity.

**Citta, manas, vijñāna.** For the Sarvāstivāda these are three names of one entity; for Yogācāra the three names apply to all eight consciousnesses but most aptly the eighth is citta, the seventh manas, the first six vijñāna. Either way they are all on the "mind" side, not mental factors.

quotes.text: 恒依心起，與心相應，繫屬於心，故名心所，如屬我物，立我所名。心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相，助成心事，得心所名。如畫師、資，作模、填彩。
quotes.note_en: Because they always arise dependent on mind, are associated with mind and bound to mind, they are called mental factors, as things belonging to me are called "mine". Mind grasps only the general characteristic of its object; mental factors grasp particular characteristics too, helping accomplish mind's work — like a master painter and apprentices, one outlining, the others colouring.

quotes.text: 心意識體一，心心所有依，有緣有行相，相應義有五。
quotes.note_en: Citta, manas and vijñāna are one in essence. Mind and mental factors have a basis, have an object, have a mode of apprehension, and are associated — "association" has five senses.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》的畫師喻，心所的作用相當於？
questions.q_en: In the Cheng weishi lun's painter simile, what do mental factors do?
questions.explain_zh: 「如畫師、資，作模、填彩」——心如畫師作模，心所如弟子填彩。
questions.explain_en: Mind is the master drawing the outline; mental factors are apprentices filling in colour.

questions.q_zh: 心與心所各取對象的什麼？
questions.q_en: What do mind and mental factors each grasp of the object?

options.zh: 心唯取總相，心所亦取別相
options.en: Mind only the general characteristic; factors particular ones too
Mind the particular, factors the general

questions.explain_zh: 「心於所緣，唯取總相；心所於彼，亦取別相。」
questions.explain_en: "Mind grasps only the general characteristic; mental factors also grasp particular characteristics."

questions.q_zh: 在百法中，八識屬於「心法」，不屬於心所。
questions.q_en: In the hundred dharmas, the eight consciousnesses are "mind" dharmas, not mental factors.
questions.explain_zh: 百法第一「心法」八種即八識；心所有法五十一種另列。
questions.explain_en: The first category, "mind", consists of the eight consciousnesses; the 51 factors are a separate category.

questions.q_zh: 下列何者**不是**《成唯識論》所說心所的條件？
questions.q_en: Which is NOT one of the Cheng weishi lun's conditions for a mental factor?
questions.explain_zh: 心所必依心而起，不能獨自生起。
questions.explain_en: Mental factors always depend on mind and cannot arise alone.

questions.q_zh: 《俱舍論》如何看心、意、識？
questions.q_en: How does the Abhidharmakośa view citta, manas and vijñāna?
questions.explain_zh: 「心意識體一」；「集起故名心，思量故名意，了別故名識」。
questions.explain_en: "Citta, manas, vijñāna are one in essence" — named by accumulating, deliberating, discerning.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》「隨勝顯」之說，哪一識最名為「意」？
questions.q_en: By the Cheng weishi lun's "named by prominence", which consciousness is most aptly called manas?
questions.explain_zh: 「第七名意，緣藏識等，恒、審思量，為我等故。」注意：第六「意識」的「意」是指其所依根，並非「最名為意」。
questions.explain_en: "The seventh is called manas: taking the store-consciousness as object, it constantly and intently deliberates, [taking it] as self." Note: the "mano-" of the sixth consciousness refers to its basis, not to this naming.

comparisons.summary_zh: 兩者都是對過惡的羞恥，差別在羞恥的依據：慚依「自」與「法」（向內），愧依「世間」（向外）。反面是無慚、無愧。
comparisons.summary_en: Both are shame at wrongdoing; they differ in what the shame relies on — hrī on oneself and the Dharma (inward), apatrāpya on the world (outward). Their opposites are the two intermediate secondary afflictions.

cells.zh: 自力、法力（自增上、法增上）

cells.en: Counters lack of self-respect; stops misconduct
Counters lack of decorum; stops misconduct

cells.zh: 向內：對不起自己與正法
cells.en: Inward: letting down oneself and the Dharma

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**共同點**：慚與愧的作用完全相同——「止息惡行為業」，而且都對「所作罪」生羞恥。

**差別在「依」**：《成唯識論》說慚「依自、法力」，愧「依世間力」。一個人不做壞事，可能是因為「這不是我這樣的人該做的、違背我所學的法」（慚），也可能是因為「別人會怎麼看我」（愧）。前者向內，後者向外。

**為何要兩個**：只靠內在的自尊，可能自以為是；只靠外在的眼光，沒人看見時就放縱。佛陀稱二者為「護世間」的「二淨法」，缺一不可。

**反面**：無慚「不顧自、法」，無愧「不顧世間」；二者遍於一切不善心，是中隨煩惱，《成唯識論》判為實有。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**In common**: their function is identical — "stopping misconduct" — and both feel shame at wrong done.

**The difference is the basis**: the Cheng weishi lun says hrī "relies on the power of oneself and the Dharma", apatrāpya "on the power of the world". One may refrain from wrong because "this is unworthy of who I am and contrary to the Dharma I follow" (hrī), or because "what would others think?" (apatrāpya). Inward versus outward.

**Why both**: self-respect alone can become self-righteous; concern for others' opinion alone lapses when no one is watching. The Buddha calls them "two pure dharmas that protect the world" — both are needed.

**Opposites**: lack of self-respect "disregards oneself and the Dharma", lack of decorum "disregards the world"; both accompany every unwholesome mind (intermediate secondary afflictions) and are ruled to be real.

quotes.text: 有二淨法，能護世間。何等為二？所謂慚、愧。
quotes.note_en: There are two pure dharmas that protect the world. What are the two? Namely, self-respect and decorum.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，「愧」所依的是什麼力量？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what does apatrāpya rely on?
questions.explain_zh: 慚「依自、法力」，愧「依世間力」。
questions.explain_en: Hrī relies on oneself and the Dharma; apatrāpya on the world.

questions.q_zh: 慚與愧的「業」（作用）相同，都是止息惡行。
questions.q_en: Hrī and apatrāpya have the same function — stopping misconduct.
questions.explain_zh: 兩者都是「止息惡行為業」，差別只在所依與體性。
questions.explain_en: Both have "stopping misconduct" as function; they differ in basis and nature.

questions.q_zh: 某人獨處無人看見時也不肯做虧心事，主要是哪一心所的作用？
questions.q_en: Someone refuses to do wrong even when completely alone and unseen. Which factor is chiefly at work?
questions.explain_zh: 無人看見時仍不作惡，是依自身與正法而羞恥——慚。
questions.explain_en: Refraining when unseen relies on oneself and the Dharma — self-respect.

questions.q_zh: 無慚、無愧屬於哪一類隨煩惱？
questions.q_en: Which class of secondary afflictions do lack of self-respect and lack of decorum belong to?
questions.explain_zh: 「無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱。」
questions.explain_en: "The two beginning with lack of self-respect pervade all unwholesome minds, hence intermediate."

questions.q_zh: 佛陀稱慚與愧為「能護世間」的二淨法。
questions.q_en: The Buddha called hrī and apatrāpya the two pure dharmas that protect the world.
questions.explain_zh: 《雜阿含經》：「有二淨法，能護世間……所謂慚、愧。」
questions.explain_en: Saṃyuktāgama: "There are two pure dharmas that protect the world … self-respect and decorum."

comparisons.title_en: The eleven wholesome factors and what each counteracts
comparisons.summary_zh: 每一個善心所都「對治」一個煩惱：信↔不信、精進↔懈怠、慚↔無慚、愧↔無愧、無貪↔貪、無瞋↔瞋、無癡↔癡、輕安↔惛沈、不放逸↔放逸、行捨↔掉舉、不害↔害。
comparisons.summary_en: Each wholesome factor counteracts an affliction: faith ↔ faithlessness, diligence ↔ laziness, self-respect ↔ its lack, decorum ↔ its lack, non-greed ↔ greed, non-hatred ↔ aversion, non-delusion ↔ delusion, pliancy ↔ torpor, conscientiousness ↔ heedlessness, equanimity ↔ restlessness, non-harming ↔ harmfulness.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一一相對**：《成唯識論》在每個善心所的定義中都明說「對治」什麼：信「對治不信」、精進「對治懈怠」、輕安「對治惛沈」、行捨「對治掉舉」……這使十一善心所成為一套完整的「解藥清單」。

**三個假立的**：不放逸與行捨都是「精進、三根」在不同作用上的假立——防惡修善叫不放逸，令心平等正直叫行捨；不害是「無瞋」在不損惱有情上的假立。其餘八個是實有。

**對照放逸**：放逸也是假立的——「由懈怠及貪、瞋、癡……總名放逸」，與不放逸的「精進＋三善根」恰好一一相反。

**怎麼用**：修行時發現自己惛沈，就修輕安（調身調息、令身心輕快）；發現掉舉，就修行捨（放下、平等）；發現懈怠，就修精進——並以信作為一切的起點。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Point by point**: in defining each wholesome factor the Cheng weishi lun says what it counteracts: faith "counteracts faithlessness", diligence "laziness", pliancy "torpor", equanimity "restlessness"… The eleven thus form a complete "list of antidotes".

**Three designated ones**: conscientiousness and equanimity are both "diligence and the three roots" named by different functions — guarding against evil and cultivating good is conscientiousness, making the mind even and upright is equanimity; non-harming is non-hatred named for not injuring beings. The other eight are real.

**Mirror image**: heedlessness is also designated — "laziness together with greed, hatred and delusion … collectively called heedlessness" — the exact inverse of conscientiousness's "diligence plus the three wholesome roots".

**Using it**: noticing torpor, cultivate pliancy (settling body and breath, lightening body and mind); noticing restlessness, cultivate equanimity (letting go, evenness); noticing laziness, cultivate diligence — with faith as the starting point of everything.

questions.q_zh: 輕安對治的是？
questions.q_en: Pliancy counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 輕安「對治惛沈，轉依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Pliancy "counteracts torpor".

questions.q_zh: 行捨對治的是？
questions.q_en: Equanimity counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 行捨「對治掉舉，靜住為業」。
questions.explain_en: Equanimity "counteracts restlessness".

questions.q_zh: 下列哪一個善心所是依「無瞋」假立的？
questions.q_en: Which wholesome factor is designated on non-hatred?
questions.explain_zh: 論中說不害是「即無瞋」，於有情不為損惱而假立。
questions.explain_en: Non-harming is non-hatred, designated for not injuring beings.

questions.q_zh: 不放逸與行捨都是依精進與三善根假立的。
questions.q_en: Conscientiousness and equanimity are both designated on diligence and the three wholesome roots.
questions.explain_zh: 兩者定義都以「精進、三根」開頭。
questions.explain_en: Both definitions begin with "diligence and the three roots".

questions.q_zh: 精進對治的是？
questions.q_en: Diligence counteracts…
questions.explain_zh: 精進「對治懈怠，滿善為業」。
questions.explain_en: Diligence "counteracts laziness, fulfilling the good".

questions.q_zh: 十一善心所中有幾個是假立的？
questions.q_en: How many of the eleven wholesome factors are designated rather than real?
questions.explain_zh: 不放逸、行捨、不害三者假立，其餘八者實有。
questions.explain_en: Conscientiousness, equanimity and non-harming; the other eight are real.

comparisons.summary_zh: 慢是「和別人比」而高舉（根本煩惱，以比較為核心）；憍是對自己的盛事陶醉（隨煩惱，貪的一分），不必比較。
comparisons.summary_en: Pride exalts oneself by comparison with others (a root affliction); haughtiness is intoxication with one's own fortune (a secondary affliction, part of greed), needing no comparison.

cells.en: Relying on self over others — comparison
Attached to one's own flourishing — intoxication

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**比較 vs 陶醉**：慢的定義是「恃己於他，高舉為性」——一定有一個「他」作比較：我比你強、我和你一樣（其實不如）、我雖不如你但也差不多……所以有七慢之分。憍則是「於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性」：對自己的年輕、健康、財富、才華感到陶醉，不需要與誰比較。

**根本與分支**：慢是六根本煩惱之一；憍是小隨煩惱，「貪愛一分為體」——本質上是對自身所有的貪著。

**最深的慢**：我慢（asmimāna），即執五取蘊為我而心高舉，與第七末那識恆時相應，直到修道斷盡。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Comparison vs intoxication**: pride is "relying on oneself, holding oneself high over others" — there is always an "other": I am better than you, I am your equal (though not), I am a bit less but still… — hence the seven kinds. Haughtiness is "deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride": delight in one's youth, health, wealth or talent, with no comparison needed.

**Root and branch**: pride is one of the six root afflictions; haughtiness is a minor secondary affliction with "a part of greed" as substance — at bottom, attachment to what one has.

**The deepest pride**: the pride of "I am" (asmimāna), taking the aggregates as self; it constantly accompanies the seventh consciousness, manas, until uprooted on the path.

quotes.text: 云何為慢？恃己於他，高舉為性；能障不慢，生苦為業。
quotes.note_en: What is pride? Relying on oneself, its nature is holding oneself high over others; its function is to obstruct humility and produce suffering.

quotes.text: 云何為憍？於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲為性；能障不憍，染依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is haughtiness? Its nature is deep attachment to one's own flourishing, intoxicated pride; its function is to obstruct non-haughtiness and be the basis of defilement.

questions.q_zh: 一個人獨處時，對著鏡子欣賞自己的年輕美貌而陶醉——這主要是？
questions.q_en: Alone in front of a mirror, someone is intoxicated with their own youth and looks. This is chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 憍是「於自盛事，深生染著，醉傲」，不必與他人比較。
questions.explain_en: Haughtiness is intoxication with one's own flourishing, with no comparison needed.

questions.q_zh: 「我的修行比他高多了」——這是？
questions.q_en: "My practice is far above his." This is…
questions.explain_zh: 與他人比較而高舉，是慢。
questions.explain_en: Exalting oneself by comparison is pride.

questions.q_zh: 憍的體性是貪愛的一分。
questions.q_en: Haughtiness has a part of greed as its substance.
questions.explain_zh: 「此亦貪愛一分為體，離貪無別憍相用故。」
questions.explain_en: "This too has a part of greed as substance."

questions.q_zh: 未證得聖果卻自以為已證得，屬七慢中的哪一種？
questions.q_en: Thinking one has attained a realization one has not reached is which of the seven kinds of pride?
questions.explain_zh: 增上慢：「於未得增上殊勝所證法中謂我已得。」
questions.explain_en: Conceit of attainment: "claiming to have attained a superior realization not yet reached."

questions.q_zh: 哪一種慢與第七末那識恆時相應？
questions.q_en: Which kind of pride constantly accompanies the seventh consciousness, manas?
questions.explain_zh: 末那識恆與我癡、我見、我慢、我愛四煩惱相應。
questions.explain_en: Manas is always accompanied by self-delusion, self-view, self-pride and self-love.

comparisons.title_en: Concealment, deceit, guile — three kinds of deception
comparisons.summary_zh: 覆是藏起自己「有」的過失；誑是假裝自己「有」其實沒有的德行；諂是為了籠絡他人而扭曲自己、曲意逢迎。三者皆以貪、癡為體。
comparisons.summary_en: Concealment hides faults one has; deceit feigns virtues one lacks; guile twists oneself to ensnare others. All three are parts of greed and delusion.

cells.en: Puts on manners to net others
Fear of losing gain and fame
Part of greed and delusion (one view: delusion)

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一藏、一裝、一曲**：覆是「減法」——把自己有的過失藏起來；誑是「加法」——把自己沒有的德行裝出來；諂則是「變形」——為了討好、籠絡他人而扭曲自己的言行，心術險曲。

**動機都與名利有關**：覆「恐失利、譽」，誑「為獲利譽」，所以都含有貪的成分；又不明白這樣做只會增長過患，所以含有癡的成分。三者都是小隨煩惱，「定是假有」。

**後果**：覆的人日後內心悔惱；誑的人走上邪命；諂的人則聽不進師友的正直教誨，因為他總在揣摩對方、掩飾自己。修行的對治是「發露懺悔」與質直心。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Hide, fake, twist**: concealment "subtracts" — hiding faults one has; deceit "adds" — displaying virtues one lacks; guile "distorts" — bending one's words and manners to please or ensnare others.

**All motivated by gain and fame**: concealment fears losing them, deceit seeks them — hence greed; not seeing that this only multiplies harm — hence delusion. All three are minor secondary afflictions, "definitely designated".

**Consequences**: the concealer is later gnawed by remorse; the deceiver slides into wrong livelihood; the guileful cannot take in the straightforward counsel of teachers and friends, being always calculating and covering. The remedy is open confession and a straightforward mind.

quotes.text: 云何為誑？為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；能障不誑，邪命為業。
quotes.note_en: What is deceit? For the sake of profit and fame, its nature is feigning virtue with trickery; its function is to obstruct non-deceit and lead to wrong livelihood.

quotes.text: 此亦貪、癡一分為體，離二無別諂相用故。
quotes.note_en: This too has a part of greed and delusion as substance; apart from these two there is no characteristic or function of guile.

questions.q_zh: 犯了錯卻不讓人知道，怕名聲受損——這是？
questions.q_en: One has done wrong but keeps it hidden for fear of one's reputation. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 覆：「於自作罪，恐失利、譽，隱藏為性。」
questions.explain_en: Concealment: "hiding one's own wrongdoing for fear of losing gain and reputation."

questions.q_zh: 明明沒有修行功夫，卻裝出很有德行的樣子以獲得供養——這是？
questions.q_en: With no real practice, one poses as virtuous to receive offerings. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 誑：「為獲利譽，矯現有德，詭詐為性；……邪命為業。」
questions.explain_en: Deceit: "to obtain profit and fame, feigning virtue … wrong livelihood."

questions.q_zh: 為了討好上司而刻意逢迎、說違心話——這是？
questions.q_en: To please the boss one fawns and says things one does not mean. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 諂：「為網他故，矯設異儀，險、曲為性。」
questions.explain_en: Guile: "to net others, contriving unusual manners; crooked."

questions.q_zh: 誑與諂都以貪、癡的一分為體。
questions.q_en: Deceit and guile both have parts of greed and delusion as their substance.
questions.explain_zh: 論中說誑、諂皆「貪、癡一分為體，離二無別……相用」。
questions.explain_en: Both are "parts of greed and delusion".

questions.q_zh: 哪一個的「業」是「邪命」？
questions.q_en: Which one has "wrong livelihood" as its function?
questions.explain_zh: 誑以詐現有德謀取利養，所以「邪命為業」。
questions.explain_en: Deceit wins offerings by feigned virtue, hence wrong livelihood.

comparisons.title_zh: 瞋的五種分位：忿、恨、惱、嫉、害
comparisons.title_en: Five faces of aversion — wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy, harmfulness
comparisons.summary_zh: 忿、恨、惱、嫉、害都「以瞋恚一分為體」，沒有獨立實體，是瞋在不同情境下的表現：當下爆發、事後積怨、惡言螫人、見人好而妒、無悲而損惱。
comparisons.summary_en: Wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy and harmfulness all "have a part of aversion as substance" — no separate entity, just aversion in different situations — erupting now, festering later, stinging with words, begrudging others' success, tormenting without compassion.
comparisons.explanation_zh:
**同一根源**：《成唯識論》對五者都說「此即（亦）瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿（恨……）相用故」。它們是小隨煩惱，各別生起，「定是假有」——只是給瞋在特定情境下的面貌取了名字。

**時間序列：忿 → 恨 → 惱**。當下怒氣爆發是忿；忿過之後怨氣不散是恨；恨積在心，追憶往事、觸動舊怨，於是惡言相向是惱。

**對象不同：嫉與害**。嫉是見他人榮盛而不能忍受；害是對有情心無悲愍、加以逼惱。論中說「瞋、害別相，准善應說」——比照無瞋（與樂）與不害（拔苦）：瞋障慈，害障悲。

**修行意義**：辨認出自己此刻是「忿」還是「恨」，就能對症：忿需當下的忍，恨需放下的慈，嫉需隨喜，害需悲心。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**One root**: for all five the Cheng weishi lun says "it has a part of aversion as substance; apart from aversion it has no characteristic or function". They are minor secondary afflictions, arising separately and "definitely designated" — names for aversion's face in particular situations.

**A time sequence: wrath → resentment → spite.** Anger erupting now is wrath; lingering after it, resentment; brooding over old grievances until they burst out in cruel words, spite.

**Different objects: jealousy and harmfulness.** Jealousy cannot bear others' success; harmfulness torments beings for lack of compassion. The treatise says their distinction from aversion "follows the wholesome": as non-hatred gives happiness and non-harming removes suffering, aversion obstructs loving-kindness and harmfulness obstructs compassion.

**For practice**: recognizing whether one is in wrath or resentment tells one the remedy — patience in the moment for wrath, letting go through kindness for resentment, sympathetic joy for jealousy, compassion for harmfulness.

quotes.text: 此即瞋恚一分為體，離瞋無別忿相用故。
quotes.note_en: It has a part of aversion as its substance; apart from aversion there is no separate characteristic or function of wrath.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，忿、恨、惱、嫉、害的共同體性是什麼？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, what do wrath, resentment, spite, jealousy and harmfulness share as substance?
questions.explain_zh: 五者都是「瞋恚一分為體」。
questions.explain_en: All five have "a part of aversion" as substance.

questions.q_zh: 被人當眾羞辱，當下怒火中燒、想要動手——這是？
questions.q_en: Insulted in public, one flares up on the spot and wants to strike. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 「依對現前不饒益境，憤發為性……執杖為業。」
questions.explain_en: "Flaring up at a present unbeneficial object … taking up the stick."

questions.q_zh: 事隔多年，一想起那人就耿耿於懷、無法釋懷——這是？
questions.q_en: Years later, one still cannot let go whenever one thinks of that person. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 「由忿為先，懷惡不捨，結怨為性。」
questions.explain_en: "Preceded by wrath, holding on to malice, binding enmity."

questions.q_zh: 同事升職，自己心中酸楚、悶悶不樂——這是？
questions.q_en: A colleague is promoted and one feels sour and gloomy. This is…
questions.explain_zh: 嫉：「不耐他榮，妬忌為性……憂慼為業。」
questions.explain_en: Jealousy: "unable to bear others' glory … its function is gloom."

questions.q_zh: 慳也是瞋恚的一分。
questions.q_en: Stinginess is also a part of aversion.
questions.explain_zh: 慳與憍是「貪愛一分為體」。
questions.explain_en: Stinginess and haughtiness are parts of greed.

questions.q_zh: 「忿→恨→惱」的順序，最後的「惱」通常表現為？
questions.q_en: In the sequence wrath → resentment → spite, how does spite usually show itself?
questions.explain_zh: 惱「䖧螫為業」，《五蘊論》說「發暴惡言尤䖧為性」。
questions.explain_en: Spite "stings"; the Pañcaskandhaka: "uttering violent, abusive words".

comparisons.title_en: Saṃskāra vs. cetanā — and the three senses of 行
comparisons.summary_zh: 思是行蘊中「最勝」的一個心所，但行蘊不等於思；十二因緣的「行」是思所發動的業；「諸行」則是一切有為法。
comparisons.summary_en: Volition is the foremost single factor within the formations aggregate, but the aggregate is not volition; the saṃskāra of the twelve links is karma set in motion by volition; "all saṃskāras" means all conditioned things.

cells.zh: 受、想以外的一切心所＋心不相應行（百法中 49＋24＝73 法）
cells.en: All mental factors except feeling & perception + non-associated formations (49 + 24 = 73 in Yogācāra)

cells.zh: 「思謂令心造作為性」（成唯識論）

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一、思是行蘊的「代表」，不是「全部」。** 《雜阿含經》以「六思身」定義行蘊，容易讓人以為行蘊＝思。但阿毗達磨指出：行蘊涵蓋受、想以外的所有心所（如信、貪、念、慧……）以及心不相應行（如得、命根、生、住、異、滅）。佛只舉「思」，是舉其最勝：「行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝」（《俱舍論》）。

**二、層次不同。** 思是一個具體的法（dharma）；行蘊是一個分類（蘊＝聚）。思必定屬於行蘊，但行蘊中的大多數法都不是思。

**三、遍行與業。** 思是遍行，每一念心都有；同時思是業的本體（「思即是意業」）。所以每一念心都帶有業性的造作傾向——這正是行蘊以「造作」為名的原因。

**四、與十二因緣之「行」。** 十二因緣的「行」是身、口、意三業，由思發動：意業就是思本身，身語業是「思已業」。行蘊描述的是當下這一念心的構成要素；十二因緣的行則是作為招感今生之因的過去業。

**五、諸行：最廣義。** 「諸行無常」的「行」＝一切有為法，連色、受、想、識都包括在內；它與「有為」（saṃskṛta，被造作的）同根。

**口訣**：思是將軍（一個心所）；行蘊是軍隊（除受、想外所有心所與不相應行）；十二因緣的行是打過的仗（已造的業）；諸行是整個被造作的世界。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**1. Volition represents the formations aggregate; it is not the whole of it.** Because the Saṃyuktāgama defines the aggregate as "the six classes of volition", it is easy to think saṃskāra-skandha = cetanā. But Abhidharma points out that the aggregate contains every mental factor apart from feeling and perception (faith, greed, mindfulness, wisdom…) plus the non-associated formations (acquisition, life-faculty, arising, duration, decay, cessation). The Buddha names volition as the foremost: "saṃskāra means forming; volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — hence foremost" (Abhidharmakośa).

**2. Different levels.** Cetanā is one specific dharma; the formations aggregate is a category ("heap"). Volition always belongs to the formations aggregate, but most dharmas in that aggregate are not volition.

**3. Omnipresent and karmic.** Volition is omnipresent — in every moment of mind — and it is also the essence of karma ("volition is mental karma"). So every moment of mind carries a karmic, forming tendency; this is why the aggregate is named "forming".

**4. The saṃskāra of the twelve links** is bodily, verbal and mental karma, set in motion by volition: mental karma is volition itself, bodily and verbal karma are "karma after having willed". The aggregate describes the components of a present moment of mind; the second link describes past karma as the cause projecting this life.

**5. "All saṃskāras" — the widest sense.** In "all saṃskāras are impermanent", saṃskāra = every conditioned dharma, including form, feeling, perception and consciousness; it shares its root with saṃskṛta, "that which is formed".

**Mnemonic**: volition is the general (one factor); the formations aggregate is the army (every factor except feeling and perception, plus the non-associated formations); the second link is the battles already fought (karma done); all saṃskāras is the whole world that has been built.

quotes.text: 然薄伽梵於契經中說六思身為行蘊者，由最勝故。所以者何？行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝。
quotes.note_en: The Blessed One described the formations aggregate in the sūtra as the six classes of volition because volition is foremost. Why? Saṃskāra means "forming"; volition, being of the nature of karma, is strongest in forming — therefore foremost.

quotes.text: 世別由業生，思及思所作，思即是意業，所作謂身語。
quotes.note_en: The variety of the world is born of karma — volition and what volition produces. Volition is mental karma; what it produces is bodily and verbal karma.

questions.q_zh: 《雜阿含經》以「六思身」定義行蘊。《俱舍論》如何解釋？
questions.q_en: The Saṃyuktāgama defines the formations aggregate as "the six classes of volition". How does the Abhidharmakośa explain this?

options.en: The aggregate consists of volition alone

options.zh: 思在行蘊諸法中造作義最強，故舉思為代表
options.en: Volition is strongest in "forming" among its members, so it is named as representative
The other mental factors belong to the feeling aggregate

questions.explain_zh: 「行名造作，思是業性造作義強，故為最勝。」行蘊實際包括色受想識以外的一切有為法。
questions.explain_en: "Saṃskāra means forming; volition … is strongest in forming, hence foremost." The aggregate actually includes all conditioned dharmas other than form, feeling, perception and consciousness.

questions.q_zh: 行蘊就等於「思」這一個心所。
questions.q_en: The formations aggregate is the same as the single mental factor volition.
questions.explain_zh: 思只是行蘊中最勝的一法。唯識百法中行蘊攝 49 個心所與 24 個不相應行。
questions.explain_en: Volition is only the foremost member. In the hundred dharmas the aggregate contains 49 mental factors and 24 non-associated formations.

questions.q_zh: 在唯識百法中，「思」屬於行蘊。
questions.q_en: In the Yogācāra hundred dharmas, volition belongs to the formations aggregate.
questions.explain_zh: 行蘊＝除受、想外的一切心所＋不相應行；思是心所而不是受、想，所以屬行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Formations = all mental factors except feeling and perception, plus non-associated formations; volition is such a factor.

questions.q_zh: 「緣無明行」的「行」指什麼？
questions.q_en: In "ignorance conditions saṃskāra", what does saṃskāra mean?

options.en: All mental factors of the formations aggregate
The three kinds of karma — bodily, verbal, mental

questions.explain_zh: 《雜阿含經》第298經：「云何為行？行有三種——身行、口行、意行。」
questions.explain_en: SĀ 298: "What are formations? Formations are of three kinds — bodily, verbal and mental."

questions.q_zh: 「諸行無常」的「行」涵蓋什麼範圍？
questions.q_en: What does saṃskāra cover in "all saṃskāras are impermanent"?

options.zh: 一切有為法，包括色、受、想、行、識
options.en: All conditioned dharmas, including form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness

questions.explain_zh: 諸行＝有為法。涅槃是無為法，不是「行」，故三法印說「一切行無常」而說「一切法無我」。
questions.explain_en: All saṃskāras = conditioned dharmas. Nirvāṇa is unconditioned, so the seals say "all saṃskāras are impermanent" but "all dharmas are non-self".

questions.q_zh: 依唯識，下列哪一個**不**屬於行蘊？
questions.q_en: In Yogācāra, which of these does NOT belong to the formations aggregate?
questions.explain_zh: 受自成受蘊。信是善心所、命根是心不相應行，都屬行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Feeling forms its own aggregate. Faith (a wholesome factor) and life-faculty (a non-associated formation) are in the formations aggregate.

questions.q_zh: 唯識百法中，行蘊共攝多少法？
questions.q_en: How many of the hundred dharmas does the formations aggregate contain?
questions.explain_zh: 51 心所減去受、想＝49，加上 24 個心不相應行＝73。（94 是五蘊總攝的有為法數。）
questions.explain_en: 51 mental factors minus feeling and perception = 49, plus 24 non-associated formations = 73. (94 is the total of conditioned dharmas in all five aggregates.)

questions.q_zh: 「思」只在有意識地做決定時才生起。
questions.q_en: Volition arises only when one consciously makes a decision.
questions.explain_zh: 思是遍行心所，「一切心中定可得」——每一念心都有思。
questions.explain_en: Volition is omnipresent — found in every moment of mind.

questions.q_zh: 依《俱舍論》，身業、語業屬於二業中的哪一種？
questions.q_en: According to the Abhidharmakośa, bodily and verbal karma belong to which of the two karmas?
questions.explain_zh: 「思已業者謂思所作。」意業即思本身（思業）；身、語業是思所發動（思已業）。
questions.explain_en: "Karma after having willed is what volition produces." Mental karma is volition itself; bodily and verbal karma are produced by it.

questions.q_zh: 南傳阿毗達摩的行蘊（saṅkhārakkhandha）包括多少個心所？
questions.q_en: How many cetasikas make up the saṅkhārakkhandha in Theravāda Abhidhamma?
questions.explain_zh: 南傳立 52 心所，除受、想外的 50 個構成行蘊。
questions.explain_en: Theravāda has 52 cetasikas; the 50 other than feeling and perception form the formations aggregate.

comparisons.summary_zh: 念是別境心所，明記曾習之境；「不忘念即是正念」；與煩惱相應、忘失所緣的則是隨煩惱「失念」（被偷走的念）。
comparisons.summary_en: Mindfulness is an object-specific factor that clearly keeps familiar objects in mind; "non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness"; mindfulness bound up with afflictions, losing its object, is the secondary affliction "forgetfulness" (stolen mindfulness).

cells.en: Obstructs right mindfulness; basis of distraction

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一條鏈**：念 → 定 → 慧。念是「定依」，定是「智依」。失念則反過來：失念 → 散亂 → 惡慧（散亂是「惡慧所依」）。一正一反，道出修行的心理機制。

**念本身通善惡**：百法把念放在別境而不是善心所，因為記住一件事本身無所謂善惡——念念不忘仇恨，也是一種「念」。《成唯識論》說「不忘念者，即是正念」，這是念在善品中的形態。

**失念的體性**：論中三說——念一分、癡一分、俱一分；《大乘五蘊論》直接稱之為「染污念」。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**A chain**: mindfulness → concentration → wisdom. Mindfulness is "the support of concentration", concentration "the support of wisdom". Forgetfulness runs the other way: forgetfulness → distraction → wrong discernment (distraction is "the basis of wrong discernment"). Together they lay bare the psychology of practice.

**Mindfulness itself is morally variable**: the hundred dharmas place it among the object-specific, not the wholesome, factors, because remembering is in itself neither good nor bad — never forgetting a grudge is also "mindfulness". "Non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness" is its wholesome form.

**Substance of forgetfulness**: three views — part of mindfulness, part of delusion, part of both; the Pañcaskandhaka calls it "defiled mindfulness".

quotes.text: 不忘念者，即是正念。
quotes.note_en: Non-forgetful mindfulness is right mindfulness.

quotes.text: 云何失念？於諸所緣，不能明記為性；能障正念、散亂所依為業。
quotes.note_en: What is forgetfulness? Its nature is being unable to remember objects clearly; its function is to obstruct right mindfulness and be the basis of distraction.

questions.q_zh: 念的「業」（作用）是？
questions.q_en: What is the function of mindfulness?
questions.explain_zh: 念「定依為業」；定「智依為業」；欲「勤依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Mindfulness supports concentration; concentration supports wisdom; aspiration supports effort.

questions.q_zh: 失念是什麼的所依？
questions.q_en: Forgetfulness is the basis of…
questions.explain_zh: 失念「能障正念、散亂所依為業」。
questions.explain_en: Forgetfulness "obstructs right mindfulness and is the basis of distraction".

questions.q_zh: 在百法中，「念」屬於善心所。
questions.q_en: In the hundred dharmas, mindfulness is a wholesome factor.
questions.explain_zh: 念屬別境，通善惡；其善的形態是正念。
questions.explain_en: Mindfulness is object-specific and morally variable; its wholesome form is right mindfulness.

questions.q_zh: 梵語 muṣitasmṛtitā 的字面意思是？
questions.q_en: What does muṣitasmṛtitā literally mean?
questions.explain_zh: muṣita 意為「被偷」。
questions.explain_en: Muṣita means "stolen".

comparisons.title_zh: 惛沈、掉舉與睡眠——禪修的兩大障礙
comparisons.title_en: Torpor, restlessness and sleep — the two great obstacles in meditation
comparisons.summary_zh: 惛沈令心下沉，障輕安與「觀」；掉舉令心上浮，障行捨與「止」。睡眠是身不自在、心昧略的狀態（不定心所），散亂則是在對象間流蕩。
comparisons.summary_en: Torpor makes the mind sink, obstructing pliancy and insight; restlessness makes it float, obstructing equanimity and calm. Sleep is a dim, contracted state (indeterminate); distraction is drifting between objects.

cells.en: Dim and contracted; body not under control

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**一沉一浮**：禪修時心最常出的兩種毛病，一是「沉」——昏昏沉沉，心提不起來；一是「浮」——念頭紛飛，心靜不下來。前者是惛沈，後者是掉舉。《成唯識論》精確地指出它們各自所障：惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那」，掉舉「能障行捨、奢摩他」。所以止（śamatha）怕掉舉，觀（vipaśyanā）怕惛沈。

**善心所的對治**：善心所中恰有一對針對它們——輕安「對治惛沈」，行捨「對治掉舉」。

**睡眠不是惛沈**：兩者合為五蓋中的「惛沈睡眠蓋」，但惛沈是遍一切染心的大隨煩惱；睡眠則是不定心所，是「身不自在、心極闇劣」的特殊狀態。

**掉舉不是散亂**：論中說「彼令易解，此令易緣」——掉舉是在理解上浮動，散亂是在對象上轉換。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Sinking and floating**: the two commonest faults in meditation are "sinking" — dull, unable to lift the mind — and "floating" — thoughts flying, unable to settle. The first is torpor, the second restlessness. The Cheng weishi lun is precise about what each obstructs: torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā", restlessness "obstructs equanimity and śamatha". So calm fears restlessness, insight fears torpor.

**Wholesome antidotes**: the wholesome factors include a matching pair — pliancy "counteracts torpor", equanimity "counteracts restlessness".

**Sleep is not torpor**: together they form the hindrance "torpor and sleep", but torpor is a major secondary affliction in every defiled mind, whereas sleep is an indeterminate factor, a special state in which "the body is not free and the mind extremely dark and weak".

**Restlessness is not distraction**: "the former makes [the mind] change its understanding, the latter its object".

quotes.text: 云何掉舉？令心於境不寂靜為性；能障行捨、奢摩他為業。
quotes.note_en: What is restlessness? Its nature is making the mind not calm with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct equanimity and śamatha.

quotes.text: 云何惛沈？令心於境，無堪任為性；能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業。
quotes.note_en: What is torpor? Its nature is making the mind unfit with regard to its object; its function is to obstruct pliancy and vipaśyanā.

questions.q_zh: 依《成唯識論》，惛沈障礙的是？
questions.q_en: According to the Cheng weishi lun, torpor obstructs…
questions.explain_zh: 惛沈「能障輕安、毘鉢舍那為業」。
questions.explain_en: Torpor "obstructs pliancy and vipaśyanā".

questions.q_zh: 對治掉舉的善心所是？
questions.q_en: Which wholesome factor counteracts restlessness?
questions.explain_zh: 行捨「對治掉舉，靜住為業」。
questions.explain_en: Equanimity "counteracts restlessness, bringing quiet abiding".

questions.q_zh: 睡眠和惛沈一樣，都是大隨煩惱。
questions.q_en: Like torpor, sleep is a major secondary affliction.
questions.explain_zh: 睡眠是不定心所，可善可惡；惛沈才是大隨煩惱。
questions.explain_en: Sleep is indeterminate; only torpor is a major secondary affliction.

questions.q_zh: 打坐時心中不斷浮現昨天的快樂事，無法平靜——主要是？
questions.q_en: While sitting, memories of yesterday's pleasures keep bubbling up and the mind cannot settle. Chiefly…
questions.explain_zh: 掉舉令心不寂靜，論中一說「此由憶昔樂事生故」。
questions.explain_en: Restlessness makes the mind unsettled; one view says it "arises from recalling past pleasures".

questions.q_zh: 掉舉與散亂的區別，《成唯識論》如何說？
questions.q_en: How does the Cheng weishi lun distinguish restlessness from distraction?

options.zh: 掉舉令易解，散亂令易緣
options.en: restlessness changes understanding; distraction changes object

options.zh: 掉舉令易緣，散亂令易解
options.en: restlessness changes object; distraction changes understanding

questions.explain_zh: 「掉舉、散亂二用何別？彼令易解，此令易緣。」
questions.explain_en: "The former makes [the mind] change its understanding, the latter its object."

comparisons.title_en: Three classes of secondary afflictions, real and designated
comparisons.summary_zh: 小隨十（各別起）、中隨二（遍不善心）、大隨八（遍一切染心）。小十與大隨中的放逸、失念、不正知定是假有；無慚、無愧、不信、懈怠定是實有；掉舉、惛沈、散亂有假實二說。
comparisons.summary_en: Ten minor (arise separately), two intermediate (in every unwholesome mind), eight major (in every defiled mind). The ten minor plus heedlessness, forgetfulness and non-alertness are definitely designated; lack of self-respect, lack of decorum, faithlessness and laziness definitely real; restlessness, torpor and distraction disputed.

cells.zh: 忿、恨、惱、覆、誑、諂、憍、害、嫉、慳
cells.en: wrath, resentment, spite, concealment, deceit, guile, haughtiness, harmfulness, jealousy, stinginess
lack of self-respect, lack of decorum

cells.zh: 掉舉、惛沈、不信、懈怠、放逸、失念、散亂、不正知
cells.en: restlessness, torpor, faithlessness, laziness, heedlessness, forgetfulness, distraction, non-alertness

cells.zh: 不信、懈怠實；放逸、失念、不正知假；掉舉、惛沈、散亂有二說
cells.en: Faithlessness, laziness real; heedlessness, forgetfulness, non-alertness designated; the other three disputed

comparisons.explanation_zh:
**為什麼叫「隨」煩惱**：《成唯識論》：「唯是煩惱分位差別、等流性故，名隨煩惱。」它們要嘛是根本煩惱在特定情境下的「分位」（如忿是瞋的分位），要嘛是根本煩惱的「等流」（同類延續）。

**三類的判準是「範圍」**：小隨煩惱各自生起，不會同時出現（忿時不一定有嫉）；中隨二者只要是不善心就一定有；大隨八者只要是染污心（包括有覆無記）就一定有。

**中隨 vs 大隨**：差別在「有覆無記心」——例如第七末那識的心是染污但屬無記，其中有大隨煩惱，卻沒有無慚、無愧。
comparisons.explanation_en:
**Why "secondary"**: Cheng weishi lun: "They are only phases of the afflictions or outflows of the same kind, hence called secondary afflictions." They are either the root afflictions in particular situations (wrath is a phase of aversion) or their homogeneous continuations.

**The three classes are defined by scope**: minor ones arise separately, not together (wrath need not come with jealousy); the two intermediate ones are present whenever the mind is unwholesome; the eight major ones whenever it is defiled at all (including obscured-neutral minds).

**Intermediate vs major**: the difference shows in "obscured-neutral" minds — e.g. the seventh consciousness is defiled yet morally neutral; the major secondary afflictions accompany it, but not lack of self-respect and decorum.

quotes.text: 唯是煩惱分位差別、等流性，故名隨煩惱。此二十種，類別有三：謂忿等十，各別起故，名小隨煩惱；無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱；掉舉等八，遍染心故，名大隨煩惱。
quotes.note_en: Being only phases of the afflictions and outflows of the same kind, they are called secondary afflictions. These twenty are of three classes — wrath and the rest, ten, arising separately, are called minor; the two beginning with lack of self-respect, pervading all unwholesome minds, intermediate; the eight beginning with restlessness, pervading all defiled minds, major.

quotes.text: 如是二十隨煩惱中，小十、大三，定是假有；無慚、無愧、不信、懈怠定是實有；教、理成故。掉舉、惛沈、散亂三種，有義是假，有義是實。
quotes.note_en: Among these twenty secondary afflictions, the ten minor and three of the major are definitely designated; lack of self-respect, lack of decorum, faithlessness and laziness are definitely real, as established by scripture and reasoning; restlessness, torpor and distraction — some say designated, some say real.

questions.q_zh: 無慚、無愧屬於哪一類？
questions.q_en: Lack of self-respect and decorum belong to which class?
questions.explain_zh: 「無慚等二，遍不善故，名中隨煩惱。」
questions.explain_en: "The two beginning with lack of self-respect pervade unwholesome minds: intermediate."

questions.q_zh: 大隨煩惱的判準是？
